Minsterhorn lies in shambles when you arrive, its defenders devastated. Amid the wreckage, Narulu is shielding the villagers. Fighting side by side, you drive back the monsters. Narulu explains that Denvel had used the Hruga's Horn to summon a deadly storm and unleash the monsters now tearing through the village. You plan to investigate further and find a way to stop the lightning storm. Though Narulu offers to join you, you ask him to report back to Olvera in Asterleeds instead. But Narulu secretly follows you, and you have no choice but to let him come along. Following his earlier notes, you crack the Lightning Barrier and press on. Soon, Airona contacts you with a grim revelation: the Engram Anomaly stems from a disruption in the star energy flow. There's a Lightning Storm Core at the heart of the chaos. Destroy it, and the disaster ends. But it's guarded by something powerful. As you near the core, you ask Narulu to take cover inside a house. Alone, you confront a monstrous Tempest Ogre. The fight is fierce, but you prevail. Just as you strike down the beast, the Lightning Storm Core unleashes a catastrophic bolt of lightning. Narulu rushes in to shield you—at the cost of his life. When the storm clears, a Void Sigil marks where the Core once was. It turns out this was all Denvel's doing. You set off for the Statue to meet Airona.
Monthly Card Privileges in Effect

Following the priest's guidance, you and your companions arrive at the Kanamia Tribe. Someone left behind a strange letter. Following its instructions, you each set out to gather intel separately. Beneath the moonlit sky, you cross paths with a mysterious girl named Rorola, the sender of the letter. She reveals that the Kanamia Tribe's Forbidden Zone is tied to the fate of the entire plain. To earn the right to enter the Forbidden Zone, you join the Kanamia Brave Trial, hunting the fearsome Iron Fang in the dense forest and surviving a brutal gauntlet. Though you emerge victorious, the Chieftain sees through your outsider identity. At the critical moment, Rorola appears to defend you, revealing that a dire omen looms over the tribe and that you are the prophesied one destined to change its fate.

After successfully obtaining the key to the Forbidden Zone and leaving the Wander Site, you discover that the Kanamia Tribe is facing a new crisis. Another Engram Anomaly has appeared, and violent storms sweep through the tribe. The chieftain and Rorola are caught in the storm, and in the critical moment, you and your companions step up...

With the storm quelled, you are now respected by the Kanamians as the new Kanamia Brave. The gate to the Forbidden Zone finally opens, and you and your companions retrieve the Divine Legacy imbued with pure Engram, the Engram Collector. With the relic in hand, everyone sets off to prepare a counterattack. Upon coming into contact with the Engram Strength, you regain fragments of your lost memories. At that moment, your fate and that of this continent become deeply entwined once again.

To address the crisis, you first visit the Pioneer Bureau to check on Tatta but learn that he has gone missing. You and Tina follow traces of fire and eventually find him. Tatta tells everyone that the turmoil in Asterleeds is likely a distraction created by Denvel to set up the final sigil. Then, he leaves alone to investigate Dark Mist Fortress. Using Tatta's information, you deduce that the final Void Sigil may be at the Shrine entrance. You then go to the Artisan Guild to help the embattled Airona and Dorothy fend off Void Monsters. You learn that the Engram Collector must be brought near the Shrine. You later reunite with Olvera and catch up with Airona and Tina en route to the Shrine. Just before arrival, a massive transformation occurs in the city as Denvel activates the final Void Sigil. The Engram Collector is destroyed, and you absorb the scattered Engram, becoming a vessel for it. Though this grants you immense power, it puts your body at extreme risk. Despite everyone's concern, you decide to go confront Denvel. Your companions stand by you, protecting you on the way. Olvera stays behind to hold off Dark Mist Legion pursuers. Dark Mist Legion takes hostages, and Tina gets surrounded when attempting to rescue hostages. You and Airona continue the trip. At the Shrine, Airona stays to fight off more enemies, and you finally confront Denvel. You channel all the Engram to purify the Void Sigils across the plains, shattering Denvel's plot.

Though injured in the battle, Denvel remains arrogant. Tatta appears and tries to stop Denvel but is attacked. Later, he departs alone to prepare for a final clash with the Dark Mist Legion. The group decides to strike back while the Void Sigils are purified and the Dark Mist Fortress' defenses are down. Tina and Olvera prepare for battle, while you and Airona are tasked with informing the citizens. At the Town Gate Square, the public enthusiastically responds to the planned attack against Dark Mist Fortress. You speak with soldiers, adventurers, and artisans, learning their thoughts and determination. Then, you head to rejoin your companions and prepare for the offensive.

Under Darya's guidance, you and Airona bypass the checkpoint and infiltrate the Sislesa Mine through a hidden secret passage. After making your way through the pitch-black mine tunnel, you finally catch a glimpse of the sorting area, strictly controlled by the Blackstone Legion, and those abnormally radiant red, Engram-rich ores. Following the clues, you witness an even more disturbing reality: The miners have lost their minds due to the Illusory Blooms, and the Starsoul Flasks provide at best a fleeting moment of calm. At that moment, the squad launches a surprise raid to arrest people. Even the weak Navi is dragged away. You have no choice but to first hide to avoid the search, then wait for an opportunity to rescue your companion. To stop the calamity, you confront the Illusory Bloom head-on in the mine tunnel, resonating with the Stamen Crystal to shatter the illusion and collecting a new crystal. Filled with frustration and self-blame, Darya resolves to continue leading the way. And so, you turn your attention to the most heavily guarded mining cave...
Effects

You reunite with Airona on the outskirts of the mine, confirming that the giant Illusory Bloom has been reduced to an empty shell. You then meet up with Boyce, who has brought the Starsoul Flasks. Darya left a cryptic and hastily scrawled letter, suggesting that you disguise yourselves as merchants to blend in at the Bekmar Transport Station. To obtain the necessary disguises and a pass, you organize goods for a merchant in exchange for a share of his caravan's travel permit. The three of you successfully infiltrate the Transport Station but are quickly suspected due to your identities. Only after showing the Starsoul Flasks as cargo do you gain the approval of the leader, Maire. She lends you a Special Permit, but on the condition that you identify the traitor in her crew. Following the clues, you first discover that Hebard has been allowing medicine to flow to the miners, then you uncover that Dedrick has been secretly selling rockthistle seed tea to the soldiers. Finally, you confront Nevelle, who is carrying Crimson Marrow, and fight off the Blackstone Legion soldiers he summons. The evidence left after the battle points to a deeper conspiracy: Nevelle, instigated by a person in black, is colluding with the squad, intending to replace Maire and smuggle Crimson Marrow. You present your findings to Maire, who confirms that the person in black has been moving between the major caravans and the squad, constantly stirring up trouble. As the situation becomes more complex, you take the Special Permit and prepare to find Boyce, who has wandered off to clear his head, before heading to the Mustard Tavern together to continue investigating the disorder in the mine and the true whereabouts of Hruga's Horn.

With Grieg's help, you and your companions infiltrate the Mining Zone and personally witness the Blackstone Legion secretly refining and transporting Crimson Marrow. Airona deduces from this that the mastermind is not a small faction but the squad's high command, and that the person in black has very likely been colluding with them all along. The gravity of the situation makes the purpose of the investigation even clearer—this batch of ore must be prevented from falling into the hands of the person in black. However, the situation is becoming increasingly urgent. The search party is closing in, and you have no choice but to take Darya and retreat quickly through the secret passage. At this very moment, a mysterious figure appears, making the truth even more elusive...

You and your companions piece together clues from the shift change schedule and confirm that a mutiny occurred at the mine during an undocumented period. The duty rules were quietly rewritten, manpower was drastically reduced, and the whereabouts of sergeants such as Milo, Breck, and Devin are now a mystery. You first try to get the truth from Milo, who has long been corrupted by his will to survive. Then, following the clues, you find Breck, who, despite appearing to go with the flow, has left behind a key to the mine caves. Inside the mine cave, you find an anonymous journal and learn that Crimson Marrow has been mined under the Grand Duke's orders for at least a year, and that someone named Klaus was caught up in the storm for his loyalty to those orders. The clues ultimately point to Devin—only by finding this sergeant, who still supports the commander, can the fragments of the truth be pieced together, blocking the outflow of ore. Darya returns to the transfer zone first to look after the miners, while you, Airona, and Boyce follow the mine cart tracks to the Transport Station, ready to continue digging into the smuggling chain and the mastermind behind it.
Unlocked Effects

You and your companions reunite in the transfer zone, only to witness Grieg and the miners being brutally threatened by Reiner. Taylor falls, an innocent victim, and a mixture of fear and anger fills every heart. Darya, devastated by her compatriot's betrayal, is on the verge of collapse and insists on finding a more drastic way to change their fate. Boyce, however, insists on reporting the situation to the Duchy, leading to a complete break between them. In his grief, Grieg decides to lead the miners in a desperate breakout, while Airona proposes another option—for you to return to Asterleeds first to seek help. You are forced to set off in a new direction alone, while the crisis in the mine behind you continues to deepen.

Last night at 22:00, Tina's file, stored in the council hall, was stolen. At 22:10, I dispatched the Corps to find the suspect, while also having Jerrad issue a commission as a backup plan. Today at 13:30, I learned the commission was accepted. Not long after, at 13:50, Tina brought in Abeku. He confessed that he had already met with the buyer but still had a few remaining pages of the file. To find the remaining pages, I went to the Pioneer Bureau to inquire with the guide. I only obtained the clue "a powerful green-haired beautiful girl and a clear-eyed adventurer duo." Combining this with Jerrad's recent eyewitness testimony at the Festival, I believe the ones who accepted the commission were Lady Airona and her new companion. To find the remaining file pages as soon as possible, I contacted all Seabreeze Festival stall owners to help find them. I know Lady Airona dislikes trouble, and my making such a big fuss will surely annoy her. ... But for the safety of Asterleeds and Tina, please forgive me, mentor. However, five minutes later, Tina returned to the Corps. She had already brought back the file! Only after communicating with her did I understand the status of the incident on your end. I am very sorry. It was my impatience that offended the beloved Lady Airona and the respected . If there is any compensation I can offer, please do not hesitate to ask...

Float & Glide : By summoning Hero's Herb, it is as if you've grown a pair of wings, awakening the imagination to soar in the sky. When you are at a certain height above the ground, you can enter a floating state and slowly fall. The joystick can change the direction of the fall. While floating, you can switch to gliding mode to travel through the air at higher speeds. The joystick can change the direction and angle of gliding. Phantom Dash : The Wind Core, born from the hurricanes on the plains, seems to possess the ability to withstand storms. By summoning Wind Core, it seems to awaken the imagination that can break through all obstacles. The first dash propels you forward a short distance and knocks back monsters in your path. Using it again within a certain timeframe will trigger a second dash with the same effect as the first. Depending on when the second dash is used, it will also quickly restore a certain amount of summoning energy.

Each stage has three difficulty tiers: - Normal: An entry-level experience with solo and duo options, allowing team-ups with AI companions. - Hard: An advanced challenge with limited revives at the start. 5 days after the dungeon opens, players who die during the boss battle can revive via countdown or Ally assistance. - Master: An extreme challenge. Each cleared stage unlocks a higher difficulty. New difficulty levels open as the server time progresses. The higher the difficulty, the stronger the entries and monsters. Clearing higher difficulties faster increases your maximum score per dungeon. Raising your total Master Mode score earns exclusive seasonal glory rewards. Note: Hard and Master modes include a "Boss Activation Countdown." Players must complete specific objectives within the time limit to unlock the boss battle. Failing to do so results in challenge failure. Note: Deaths in the dungeon will additionally reduce the remaining time. Plan your survival strategy carefully. Solo/Dual Mode unlocks for Hard Mode, Master 1, and Master VI after the dungeon has been available for a certain number of days. Players can team up with AI companions. During boss challenges, fallen players can revive via countdown or teammate assistance. Unlock timing varies by difficulty, but rewards remain unchanged in Solo/Dual Mode.

Modification is divided into Reforge Effect Modification and Rare Effect Modification. Reforge Effect Modification: When gear reaches maximum Perfection, it can no longer be reforged. If the current reforge effects are unsatisfactory, one effect can be manually selected from the gear's reforge effect pool. Rare Effect Modification: If the current rare effect is unsatisfactory, one effect can be manually selected from the gear's rare effect pool. Some gear does not initially have a rare effect, but one can still be selected from the gear's rare effect pool through Modification. Note: 1) The Modification interface only displays gear available for the current class. Gear for other classes will only appear after switching to that class. 2) Currently, for specialization-adaptive gear, only certain special weapons can be modified. Modification results are calculated independently for each specialization. 3) Only one effect can be selected per Modification. Each Modification consumes materials separately, and consumed materials are not refunded upon dismantling. Choose entry effects carefully.

When strong emotions or spiritual elements merge with Engram and become physical, they form what's known as Imagine . On Regnus, Imagine is a common supernatural force rivaling the Legacy. Users can summon entities, weapons, or empower themselves. Its limits remain unknown. Imagine is stored in gem-like items called Imagine Seeds , which must be activated. These seeds are hard to destroy and appear randomly-no one can create or predict them.

A massive amount of thunder energy converged into a devastating thunderstorm, mercilessly striking Minsterhorn and causing irreparable damage... Even more deadly, the lingering thunder energy solidified into a barrier, blocking the way forward and making rescue efforts extremely difficult. Only by locating the source of the Engram Anomaly can this catastrophe be resolved.

The Kanamians once lived for generations along the shores of Pale Azure Lake, but the Independence War changed everything. Flames engulfed their homeland, and the tribe's living space shrank drastically. The damage ran deeper-many lives were lost, and the survivors couldn't return to bury their fallen kin. Now, the ruins are haunted by twisted Engram Aberrants , forcing the Kanamians to face the nightmare of fighting their once-loved ones if they wish to reclaim it. That bloodstained land remains an unhealed scar, a constant reminder of the pain left by the war.

The Wind, influenced by the Void Sigil, began to gather in large quantities near the Source. The congested Wind eventually formed a terrifying tornado, which struck the Kanamia Tribe. The hurricane caused severe damage, destroying the houses of the Kanamia Tribe, uprooting trees, and displacing the tribespeople...

Across the Asteria Plains, a unique group known as Scavengers roams the wilds with packs on their backs, living apart from the crowded city in their own way. The wilderness is harsh, so they often travel in small groups. Losing a companion means no one to share fire, offer herbs, or fend off beasts. Mutual support is vital. Though borders aren't formal, each group tends to stick to familiar ground. Andra Resting Post is their largest gathering spot-a place to sleep, trade goods, and share information.

Forging artisans are one of the four major disciplines within the Artisan Guild, renowned for their mastery of material processing and object creation. With Legacy forging now widespread, traditional tools like hammers have been fully replaced by Bapharian forging instruments. Modern artisans can synthesize basic materials into high-grade forging composites, used in ship keels, hardened blades, and precision components. Forging artisans have thus become the cornerstone of the artisan tradition.

A tavern built against the cliffside, with a strikingly unusual exterior. It has two levels above and below ground. The upper floor is only open to Byrnhald soldiers and serves as their sole place for leisure. The lower level is dim and sunless, meant for the miners who can rarely afford to come in. Whether due to scarce resources or some other reason, the downstairs area has no seating. Miners can only stack crates outside into makeshift stools, buying themselves a brief rest and a single drink before returning to work.

After a miner dies, their coworkers stack these stones to honor the dead. They choose each stone with care, using its texture, shape, and color to sum up a life: jagged uneven stones for passion, small smooth ones for caution, and so on. The piled heap becomes the miners' only tribute to the departed. Naming it "Astral Stone" may be their way of telling the world that those who rest here once shone like starlight beneath the darkness of the mine.

I am Totoka of the Advanced Investigation Squad. If this letter safely reaches the Guild, it means I have no other choice but to request outside assistance. We were ordered to investigate the ancient mech that appeared above the highlands. At first, everything seemed normal. Although its scale was astonishing, it appeared to be nothing more than scrap remnants of a bygone era, with only parts of its outer shell and structure still recognizable. Master Graylen concluded that it should have completely shut down long ago; Master Karst, however, became unusually excited upon seeing it, insisting it was a rare and invaluable relic. But the further we continued our investigation, the more something felt wrong. That mech is not merely simple wreckage. In the gaps of its armor, deep within its joints, and even around its core, we could clearly see traces of erosion caused by Illusory Blooms! Now, the two masters have personally ventured deep inside for quite some time. I was originally stationed outside as support, but I have waited a long time and neither has returned. ...It is my own cowardice. I dare not go in without authorization. With my abilities, I would likely just be a hindrance if I went inside. But if I keep waiting like this, I truly fear something may happen to the masters. Thus, I can only write this letter and request the Guild to send reinforcements as soon as possible. If possible, please be sure to enlist adventurers capable of handling dangerous situations. —Advanced Investigation Squad, Artisan Guild Totoka

When you read this note, I bring you glad tidings: This island now belongs to you. Make haste-travel to Ocean Hill and register its coordinates without delay. And since you've stepped onto this Misty Island, my mission may yet endure. The box with the needle attached is my flight data box-used to record all aerial parameters. In Kanamian tradition, residents construct stone towers-known as "requiem towers"-by stacking stones in memory of deceased clan members. According to legend, the taller the tower, the quicker the soul's journey to reunite with the ancestors. Due to access restrictions around the Forbidden Zone, the Zeroing Spring has become the primary site for mourning, making wishes, and brooding over memories. It is widely regarded as the second holiest location in Kanamia. Locals often inscribe the names of lost loved ones on stones and cast them into the spring or construct requiem towers nearby. Perhaps the prayers offered here may guide the beloved departed-those loved and lost-safely into the embrace of their ancestors, sparing their souls from an eternity of lonely wandering in this world...

To most people, stone means hardness and stubborn will. Call someone cold-hearted and you say they have a heart of stone. But Holmes sees it differently. Three years ago, the brilliant geologist arrived at the Bahamar Highlands, throwing himself into fieldwork with boundless passion. Through Holmes's highly romantic lens, those giant stones piercing the sky above the highland seem to radiate endless vitality. They whisper in the wind, recounting the stories of the highland across tens of thousands of years. "You must listen carefully when stones speak," Holmes often insists. And within this book, he truly acts as the bridge between humanity and the rock, allowing us to understand the stone's very soul, and the human civilization that, like a tide, has washed over them, leaving its lasting mark. (A line of messy handwriting is visible at the bottom of the title page.) Oh, so it's about listening to the stones speak. I thought it was about listening to the stones speak!

Adventurers can enhance their combat strength by equipping gear. Gear Slot: There are 11 equipment slots in total: Weapon, Helmet, Armor, Gauntlets, Boots, Necklace, Earrings, Ring, Charm, Bracelet (L), and Bracelet (R). Gear Effect: Gear effects are categorized into Basic Attributes, Advanced Attributes (which include Reforged Attribute and special Rare Attribute), and Cultivation Effects (such as refinement, embedding, and set effects, etc). Equip and Unequip Gear: Adventurers can equip, unequip, and replace gear through the Gear interface. Choose gear that suits your class/style. Gear Enhancement: At the Artisan Guild, players can reforge, refine, embed, or dismantle gear to enhance its power. Tips: Some Legendary Gear will auto-adapt based on your current style . It is recommended to prioritize equipping such gear when available.

Q: How to quickly increase character power? A: In the early and mid-game, power can be increased quickly by upgrading [Adventurer Level] , [Talents] , [Gear] , and [Battle Imagines] . As the season progresses, [Deep-Slumber Psychoscopes] and [Modules] will unlock. Q: How to increase Adventurer Level? A: The main sources of EXP are [Story Quests] and daily [Activity] rewards in the Season Hub. Completing other [Quests] also grants EXP. Q: How to develop Talents? A: The Talent system determines skill rotation and combat style. In the early game (Stage 1), basic talents help adventurers get familiar with the system. In Stage 2, a specialization path can be chosen and further developed. [Resource Acquisition] Talent Points: Gained from Adventurer Level increases, Trial Path challenges, and Talent Training quests from Airona. Seals: Obtained from Colorful Store - Honor Coin exchange, Trial Path rewards, Field Boss/Elite loot. Tips : Use the Recommended Allocation feature to quickly activate Talent nodes based on suggested plans. The guide also contains detailed explanations of different specializations. Q: How to obtain Gear? A: Lv.120 Entry-Level Epic Gear: Dropped twice daily in Unstable Space, or exchanged at Harvey's in the Artisan Guild (Gear Store) using Alloy Shards (shards obtained from Unstable Space/Honor Coin Store). Lv.120 Superior Epic Gear: Dropped in "Chaotic Realm" on Normal difficulty. Lv.120 Premium Gold Gear: Dropped in "Chaotic Realm" on Hard difficulty. As the season progresses and new dungeon content unlocks, higher-level gear becomes available. Q: How to develop Gear? A: Reforge : Use Reforge Stones to increase gear Perfection (materials from Unstable Space/Chaotic Realm/Honor Coin Store). Refine : Boost slot power; seamlessly inherited across gear (materials from Honor Coin Store/Guild Store/Life Skills). Embed : Embed gems or sigils to enhance gear stats (materials from Life Skills). Q: How to obtain and upgrade Battle Imagines? A: Battle Imagines are a core progression system that provide passive stat bonuses and powerful active skills. Craft them at the Imagine Research Institute using Wills. Wills and related materials are obtained by challenging Field Elites/Bosses, Stimen Vaults, and other game modes. Tips : Use the Monster Hunt Manual to check boss info. Q: What to do after completing the main quests? A: Make good use of the [Handbook] , [Activity] , and [Features] in the Season Hub. The daily goals in the Handbook are tailored to the Adventurer's progression, guiding them through personal development and various modules. It is highly recommended to follow them. With [Activity], Adventurers can freely choose their preferred daily events to easily acquire most resources. When unsure of what to do, check [Features] for various challenges, casual modes, and weekly activities available to Adventurers. Tip : Item tooltips feature a [Source] option. Tap it to quickly locate where items are obtained. Q: How to earn money in the game? A: Various items can be listed on the [Trading Center] to earn [Luno] . A stable way to earn money is by participating in Life Skill activities. Any items obtained by consuming [Focus] can be listed for sale. Q: Will missing a day cause a drop behind? A: New and returning Adventurers do not need to worry about falling behind after missing daily activities. [Unclaimed EXP] allows for quick catch-up by granting double EXP. Missed items can be retrieved from the [Reclaim Hub] . Rewards and challenges missed during the week can be exchanged there using Reclaim Tokens. Access it via the bottom-left corner of the [Season Hub] interface. Important Currencies and Stores Honor Coin - Honor Coin Store The Honor Coin Store provides key progression resources such as skill books, seal stones, Reforge Stones, and skill modules. It refreshes weekly. Honor Coins are the primary weekly activity currency and are obtained from daily Activity challenges, commissions, Life Skills, and Guild events. Guild Token - Guild Store The Guild Store offers refining materials, purple Will-related materials, Focus potions, and exclusive appearances. Earn Guild Tokens through weekly guild missions, guild events, daily guild sign-ins, and guild cargo. Friendship Points - Friendship Store The Friendship Store offers bound Rose Orbs, Homestead Coin Pouches, Mixing Agents, Dye Selection Packs, as well as special Namecards, Headwear, Outfits, and lots of fun emotes. Earn Friendship Points by participating in casual activities, assisting Adventurers or newbies, and increasing friendship level by interacting with friends. Mystery Store The Mystery Store refreshes daily with various contents, including skill books, Reforge Stones, refining materials, and other progression items. It also includes Star Chests, Mixing Agents, and Vault Cards. For Adventurers who want to increase power, it's recommended to spend your bound Rose Orbs in the Mystery Store for progression materials. Additionally, Adventurers can purchase cosmetics in the Personality Store, and buy specific emotes, appearances, rare materials, and multi-class unlock stones in the Orb Store.

Q: How to catch up in level? A: The main source of EXP is [Story Quests] and daily [Activity] rewards in the Season Hub. Other [Quests] also grant EXP. The daily [Activity] EXP is stored in the [Unclaimed EXP Pool] , and future EXP gains will be doubled until you've caught up. The level cap for Season 1 is 60. Returning Adventurers can quickly catch up through daily activity and main story quests. Q: How to recover lost resources? A: During your absence, the system will store missed [Daily Activity Rewards] , contents from the [Honor Coin Store] , [Unstable Space] , [Stimen Vaults] , overflowed Elite/Boss Loot Keys, and overflowed Focus. After returning, you can go to [Season Hub - Activity] and access the Reclaim Hub at the bottom left to recover them. Recovering resources helps you quickly catch up in strength. Q: How to improve strength after returning? A: Use [Unclaimed EXP] to quickly catch up on Adventurer Level, and retrieve resources from the [Reclaim Hub] . Then, use [Alloy Shards] to exchange for gear, and enhance it using recovered Reforge Stones and refining materials. Use recovered skill books and Imprint materials to develop your skills and talents, boosting your strength. Tips : For more detailed progression guidance, refer to the [Must-Read for Newbies] section. Q: Can I participate in gameplay before catching up in strength? A: Most gameplay modes that provide resources can be completed solo and do not require high strength. Examples include: Daily Missions, Unstable Space, Field Elite/Boss hunts, and Life Skills. In addition, as the season progresses, Chaotic Realm will offer AI Assistance mode for various difficulties to help Adventurers continue progressing in gear. Meanwhile, once strength improves, Stimen Vaults can also be challenged at higher floors (solo challenge allowed). Overall, after returning, Adventurers can participate in most content through solo activity and gradually catch up with the main group to resume regular play. Tips : For information on Adventurer Level, progression systems, earning money, currencies, and key stores, please check the [Must-Read for Newbies] section.

Once the event begins, monster hordes will appear near all elite monster areas in the Highlands and remain for 10 minutes. Thanks to Happy's support, the monsters' defense will be greatly reduced, so adventurers need not fear the incoming horde! This event and "Natsu's Trial" share a weekly cap of 2,000 Adventure Bond Proofs in total.

Consumes 5 Ice Energy to instantly summon 3 Meteor Storms above the target, dealing Magic Damage to the target and surrounding enemies. This skill holds 2 charges. Tips: This instant-cast DMG skill is best utilized in a highly mobile style of combat to maximize DMG dealt through repeated use.

Unleashes built-up cold energy in a violent surge, dealing Magic Damage and inflicting Frozen on nearby enemies. Charging the skill alters both its range and DMG. Tier 1 : Chants for 1 s, targeting an 8 m frontal cone. Tier 2 : Chants for 2 s, targeting an 8 m frontal cone with 50% increased DMG. Tier 3 : Chants for 3 s, targeting an 8 m frontal cone with 100% increased DMG. When holding 1 / 3 / 5 Frost Crystal , the skill will instantly cast at Tier 1 / 2 / 3 , skipping the charge time. Tips: This skill offers both area damage and crowd control. For best results, cast it when you have high Frost Crystal count.

Consumes 15 Ice Energy to launch a concentrated ice beam toward the target, dealing Magic Damage to all enemies in its path every 0.3s . After dealing DMG 5 instances, the beam attempts to consume additional Ice Energy to sustain itself. Every 12 Ice Energy extends the beam by 0.3s and deals 1 additional instance of DMG. Each time Frostbeam deals DMG, it increases its own DMG by 8% , up to 80% . (Terminates when Ice Energy drops below 3 .) Frostbeam 's firing interval is affected by Haste. Tips: Cast when Ice Energy is near maximum capacity for extended beam duration. While firing, use the joystick to make minor positioning adjustments.

Chants for 1.4s , then consumes 10 Ice Energy to fire a sharp Frost Lance at the target, dealing Magic Damage on impact. Consuming 1 Frost Crystal can skip chanting and increase DMG by 20% . Tips: Cast Frost Lance regularly to avoid wasting excess Energy.

Summons the power of frost, gaining Super Armor for the duration while accumulating 6 Ice Energy per second and increasing Haste . Tips: Increases Attack SPD and Casting SPD. Since this skill generates Ice Energy, don't use it when Ice Energy is about to cap. If you do, burn the Ice Energy quickly afterward.

Chants for 2.9s , then consumes 20 Ice Energy to summon an intense Blizzard at the target location, continuously dealing Magic DMG and applying Frost to all enemies within the area. Tips: This devastating AoE skill is most effective when used against immobilized enemies to maximize DMG dealt.

Encases yourself in ice, rendering you immune to all DMG but immobilized for the duration. Deals Magic Damage to all nearby enemies, and inflicts Slow until they are Frozen . Tips: Equip this skill in high-pressure situations to increase survivability.

Summons a surging Tidal Vortex at the target location, dealing Magic DMG on impact. Channels for 5s after casting. Recast to end early. Ultra Cold: Tidepool In the Ultra Cold state, the vortex freezes and violently explodes upon ending, dealing higher Magic DMG to all enemies within range. Tips: You cannot move or cast other skills while channeling. Best paired with allies' AoE skills in coordinated attacks.

Summons the ice's blessing to unfold an Ice Domain , knocking all enemies back within range. Then summons a comet to strike the targets, dealing Magic DMG and inflicting Frozen on all affected enemies. Ice Domain Within the Domain, restores 220 Ice Energy over time and gains Ultra Cold . Enemies within the domain are continuously Slowed until Frozen . While in Ultra Cold , targets are treated as Frozen . Tips: Don't use this skill when Ice Energy is about to cap. If you do, burn the Ice Energy quickly afterward. Skills enhanced by the Ultra Cold state are most effective when cast within this skill's duration.

Raises the banner spear, granting Inspire to allies. Afterward, a follow-up leap can be launched, dealing Attack DMG to the enemies within range and knocking them airborne , while restoring 100 Courage . Inspire : Lasts for 10s . During this time, all allies' Haste + 10% . You restore 10 Courage per second and 1 stack of Sharp every 2s . "Endless storm, unlock thy mighty power at my knight's command! Wind, reveal thy glory with a surging rush! Manifest in the wind! Tips: Cast when Courage is low.

Consumes 2 stacks of Sharp to leap into the air and deliver a powerful aerial strike, dealing Attack DMG . Tips: Combo with Skyward Spec. Cast when Courage is low to prevent overcapping and wasting Courage regeneration.

Consumes 40 Courage to leap into the air and hurl a wind-forged spear with force. Deals Attack DMG to all enemies in range and greatly reduces their Resilience. Grants 1 stack of Sharp . Tips: Effective against enemies with Resilience. Also recommended when dealing with multiple targets.

Converts Courage into a sustained wind field, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies until Courage runs out, using 16 Courage per second. The skill may be deactivated by clicking again. Tips: Cast at full Courage and regain Courage during Valor Cyclone to extend duration.

Leaps into the air and crashes down, dealing massive Attack DMG to the target and surrounding enemies. Each stack of Sharp consumed charges the skill for 5% . Tips: Sharp Impact deals massive DMG. Consume as much Sharp as possible within a fixed time window to maximize DMG.

Enhanced Falcon Toss , leap into the air and gather wind power , launching a fierce wind blade spear. Deals 750% ATK as Attack DMG to all enemies in the area and significantly reduces their tenacity, growing with the upgrade/advancement of the Falcon Toss skill. Immediately gain 3 stacks of Sharp after Casting .

After dealing 6 instances of DMG, gains 1 stack of Battle Will . Battle Will : A manifestation of fierce will. Grants a Shield upon gaining, with 20% base DMG Reduction. Pro Tips: Keep up continuous DMG to maintain the shield effect and stack Battle Will.

Performs a gentle hop, summoning vines to glide and deal Forest DMG . Bloom During the glide, casts Bloom instantly to launch 3 Dodder Seeds. Dance can be used twice in a row. Pro Tips: This is a charge-based skill-watch charge cap to avoid waste. After casting, uses Basic Attack to trigger Bloom for extra hits and 3 more Dodder Seeds

Chants for 1.8s , then consumes 30 Energy to heal the caster and up to 10 nearby allies (Party Members Prioritized). Healing grows with MATK. Tips: In emergencies, cast repeatedly for fast healing. Otherwise, use Basic Attacks to stack Regen Buds, boosting Bloom's healing.

Harnesses forest power to summon a spirit deer that charges forward, dealing massive Forest DMG to all enemies along its path. When it vanishes, it leaves behind a Fertile Domain that heals allies standing inside. "Power of the earth, heart of the forest-may the source of life never run dry!" Pro Tips: This Ultimate creates a wide rectangular area damage path and a healing zone. Pay attention to enemy placement before casting. While active, each attack skill that hits an enemy spawns a Dodder Seed-chain your skills to trigger more.

Consumes 20 Energy to summon a giant vine that strikes a target area, dealing Magic DMG and healing the caster and the nearby ally with the lowest HP (Party Members Prioritized). Healing grows with MATK. Use on demand in emergencies. For better results, pair with offensive skills to trigger Symbiotic Marks and boost effectiveness.
Consumes 30 Energy to channel a seed barrage for 5.9s , dealing Magic DMG to enemies. You can move while channeling. Tips: Great for solo play or filling DMG gaps.

Consumes 40 Energy to channel the power of forest for 4s , healing the caster and up to 10 nearby allies over time (party members prioritized). Healing scales with the caster's MATK (plus an additional fixed amount equal to 15% of the target's Max HP), and healing targets also gain 15% All Element Resistance for 10s . Tips: A strong healing skill for high-pressure moments. Since it requires channeling, time your cast carefully.

Consumes 20 Energy to imbue the caster and up to 10 nearby allies (prioritizing teammates) with the forest power for 10s , healing them every second (Interval affected by Haste). Tips: Cast after combat begins to provide steady team-wide healing over time.

Chants for 2.3s , then consumes 40 Energy to release a pulse from the caster. The pulse heals the caster and all affected allies. Tips: In AoE-heavy healing encounters, use this skill carefully to avoid wasting its dispel and putting it on CD too early.
Channels for 6 s, summoning falling seeds every 0.5s to deal magic dmg to nearby enemies. At the same time, heals up to 10 nearby allies (prioritizing teammates) and grants them 25% DMG Reduction.

Consumes 30 Energy to summon giant vines that strike a target area, dealing Magic DMG and healing the caster and the nearby ally with the lowest HP (Party Members Prioritized). Healing grows with MATK. Tips: In emergencies, cast repeatedly for fast healing. Otherwise, use Basic Attacks to stack Regen Buds, which improves both healing and DMG.

Steps forward after a brief charge to fiercely slash the target, dealing Attack DMG to the enemy and recovering 25 Flame Soul . If the attack hits the target, instantly recovers 5% of Max HP. Strategy: Intersperse this skill during damage output to effectively improve survivability. It can also be used after Wildfire Dance to replenish some HP.

With superb technique, continuously unleashes storm-like slashes on the target, dealing Attack DMG and consuming 85 Flame Soul . The skill can be cast again within 2 s of the previous instance ending, up to a maximum of 4 times. Strategy: High cost makes it unsuitable for increasing Formless level. It is usually used as the main damage dealer after Formless reaches maximum.

Wields the weapon like a whirlwind, dealing Attack DMG to targets within 3 meters. Each spin consumes 260 Stamina . Tap again while skill is active to end it. Strategy: Stamina must be reasonably allocated between damage output and survivability. When safe, it can be used more for dealing damage and increasing Formless level.

Releases power to perform a powerful leaping cleave at the target, dealing Attack DMG to enemies within 4 meters of the landing point. Upon landing, creates Crimson Earth, which deals additional Attack DMG to all enemies within 4 meters over 5s, and restores 15 Flame Soul . Tips: Use to engage targets and restore Flame Soul. Cast in advance when burst damage is needed to remain within Crimson Earth.

Consumes 50 Flame Soul to unleash a powerful cross-shaped energy slash forward. The slash travels forward for a set duration, dealing Attack DMG to all enemies along its path. 100% of the DMG dealt to the primary target is converted into HP. Also grants 50% Life Steal for a certain duration. Tips: Combine with rapid Crimson Soul Gauge buildup and gain additional recovery when HP is low.

Enhanced Unbound Meteor executes a charged leaping slash, dealing Attack DMG equal to 1,200% ATK to enemies within 4 meters of the landing point. Damage scales with the Unbound Meteor skill's levels/tiers. Recovers 15 Flame Soul . Upon landing, generates Crimson Earth, which deals additional Attack DMG to all enemies within 4 meters for 5s.

Blade Intent Stacks 2 Blade Intent per second. When fully charged, Special Attack is enhanced: Consumes 100 Blade Intent to greatly increase its casting speed. Basic Attack: Swift Justice Unleashes up to four sweeping strikes in longsword form, each dealing Attack DMG . Tips: Use the Special Attack promptly when Blade Intent reaches the max to maximize damage.

A supreme sword technique sharp enough to cut the air itself. Unleashes a flurry of slashes in front, dealing Attack Damage to all enemies in range. Grants max Thunder Sigil and fully restores Blade Intent at the end of the strike. "Heaven's weapon dims even the brightest stars." Tips: Cast when Thunder Sigil is empty to quickly charge it. Also effective against multiple targets for massive area damage.

Powers up and delivers a swift forward slash, consuming all Thunder Sigils to deal Attack Damage . Each Thunder Sigil consumed boosts DMG by 25% . "Everything I see, hear, or sense can be severed." Tips: Use when Thunder Sigils reach the max for maximum damage.

Consumes 3 Thunder Sigils to dash forward with a spinning blade attack, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies. Moonblades on the field perform a whirling slashing attack, dealing Attack DMG to surrounding targets. This damage scales with the Level/Tier of Scythe Wheel . "Under the moonlight, I move as one with the shadows." Tips: Use when multiple Moonblades exist to trigger as many whirling attacks as possible.

Consumes all Thunder Sigils to power up and dash forward, slashing all enemies along the path to deal Attack DMG . Each Thunder Sigil increases DMG by 25% . "In a blink of lightning, the blade is already unsheathed." Tips: A core skill of Iaido Slash Spec. Prioritize using it before Iaido Slash. Use when your Thunder Sigils are at their maximum to maximize damage.

Consumes all Thunder Sigils to release slashes across a wide area, dealing Attack DMG . Each Thunder Sigil increases DMG by 25% . Grants immunity to all DMG while slashing. Tips: A core skill of Iaido Slash Spec. Use when facing 3 or more targets and your Thunder Sigils are at their maximum to maximize damage.

Turns the weapon into a scythe, swinging it to perform multi-hit attacks against surrounding enemies, dealing Attack DMG and repelling enemies. The final strike inflicts a 50% Wound on the target for 10s . Summons Moonblades to aid in combat. Moonblade : Spins for 35s , dealing Attack DMG on the target every 2s . Casting Moonstrike commands all active Moonblades to release a whirling attack, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies. When you die, Moonblades end immediately and the remaining CD of Scythe Wheel is refunded. Tips: A core skill of Iaido Slash Spec. Release just prior to each Moonblade's expiration to maximize its DMG.

Phantom Scythe Wheel Approach the target at lightning speed, then creates a Phantom Scythe Wheel, dealing Thunder Element damage for 3s, striking every 0.5s. Tips: Reliable Attack skill when enemy movement is unpredictable. Great for dealing massive DMG.

Raijin Dash Use the Thunder Power to vanish into the air, then unleash rapid slashes from air, dealing multiple hits of Thunder Element damage . Tips: Grants extended Super Armor during the attack, making it an excellent option for sustained wide-area DMG.

Oblivion Combo A supreme sword technique sharp enough to cut the air itself. Unleashes a flurry of slashes in front, dealing Attack DMG to all enemies in range. Grants max Thunder Sigil and fully restores Blade Intent at the end of the strike. "Heaven's weapon dims even the brightest stars." Tips: Cast when Thunder Sigil is empty to quickly charge it. Also effective against multiple targets for massive area damage.

Enchants the blade with thunderous power. While active, any action that would grant Thunder Sigils would instantly maxes them out. Also increases ATK and grants Super Armor for the duration. Tips: Best paired with Overdrive and Talents to rapidly gain and spend Thunder Sigils, unleashing massive DMG within a short window.

Enhanced Raijin Dash , Consume all Thunder Sigil s to summon more ferocious lightning, dealing 450% ATK as Attack DMG (which scales with the Level/Tier of Raijin Dash ). Each Thunder Sigil consumed increases DMG by 25% .

Imbues the blade with thunder. During this time, gain the max number of Thunder Sigils whenever you would otherwise gain any. Also increases ATK and grants Super Armor for the duration. Tips: Best paired with Overdrive and Talents to rapidly gain and spend Thunder Sigils, unleashing massive DMG within a short window.

Adopts a defensive stance, granting immunity to all damage for its duration. If struck, executes a rapid forward slash and jumps back. Activating the skill again performs a Dashing Slash forward, dealing Attack DMG . Grants max Thunder Sigils if the attack hits a target. Tips: Using this skill in high-pressure situations or during familiar combat encounters yields a higher number of Thunder Sigils.

Basic Attack: Thunderclap Arcane Performs up to three consecutive thunder-infused strikes, each dealing Thunder Element damage . Plunge Attack:·Thunderfall from the Heavens Charges lightning energy into the gauntlet mid-air, then dives down to impact the ground, dealing Thunder Element damage on landing. Heavy Strike: Thunder Onslaught Gathers energy to unleash a powerful cannon blast. During the charge, consumes heat gauge to continuously stack Thunder Onslaught, which increases DMG and range. Releasing the skill or completing the charge unleashes a wide fan-shaped Lightning area damage . Thunderclap Increases the next Thunder Onslaught's DMG and AoE range, stacking up to 3 times. Pro Tips: When monsters are close, hold down Basic Attack to more efficiently knock them back.

Thunder Zone launches into the air and fires a Thunderstorm Bolt at the target. On hit, it deals Thunder DMG and creates a Thunderstorm Zone lasting 7s. Thunderstorm Zone deals AoE Thunder DMG every second to all enemies within the range, with a Slow debuff. Pro Tips: This skill can be cast while airborne, granting enhanced mobility during execution.

Thunder Traverse Unleashes a relentless stream of Thunder Tracers that track enemies and deal Thunder Element damage on impact. Hold the skill button to continue the barrage, consuming the heat gauge to extend its duration. Pro Tips: Best used when fully charged-hold the skill to unleash an overwhelming barrage for dealing massive DMG.

Thunderburst Oblivion Launches an Oblivion Bomb that detonates after a short flight or on impact, unleashing a destructive burst of Lightning area damage . Immediately maxes out the weapon's heat gauge upon cast. Pro Tips: Cast from a safe distance to unlock a brief window of massive Attack.

When dealing DMG, there is a chance to trigger Sigil: Lightning Chain . Sigil : Deals 1 instance of Thunder Element damage to nearby enemies, bouncing up to 4 times. Pro Tips: Strike fast when monsters are clustered so that you can start the chain reactions.

- A witty, cheerful, and proactive good guy. - Energetic, treats people with warmth and kindness, and is easy to get close to. - Usually seems carefree and unfocused, but is actually very meticulous and always perceptive of others' feelings. - (His beloved companion is a pig named Whirlwind Sweetheart.)

Cracking Echo Unleashes the Power of Rock, instantly dealing Attack DMG in a large area in the front and stunning enemies for 3s, then condenses energy to immediately gain 5 Sand Crystals . Also puts the caster into Rock's Fury state. Rock's Fury Lasts for 8s , grants Super Armor , increases Armor by 100% and Max HP by 50% , and grants 40 Rage over time. Tips: Use when facing extremely heavy incoming DMG.

Consumes 40 Rage to unleash a powerful shockwave that deals Attack DMG to all nearby enemies. When sufficient Sand Crystal is available, it is consumed to generate a Shield that absorbs all incoming DMG, lasting for 12s . For each additional Sand Crystal consumed, additional shield value is added, with a maximum of 2 Sand Crystals consumed at a time. (Shields can stack, but cannot exceed 150% of Max HP.) Tips: Casting is recommended when no shield is active to ensure continuous shield uptime.

Consumes 50 Rage and 5 Sand Crystals . Unleashes a mighty roar, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies, interrupting their actions, and granting an all-DMG-absorbing Shield . (Shields may be stacked, with a maximum capacity equivalent to 150% of maximum HP.) Reduces Attack DMG taken from the target by 10% for 12s . Tips: Provides damaging capabilities when survival pressure is minimal and grants greater Armor in situations where enemies predominantly inflict Attack DMG.

Consumes 30 Rage to swing your weapon and create a vacuum, pulling nearby enemies toward you. Deals Attack DMG , interrupts their actions, and reduces their Move SPD by 70% for 8s . Tips: Effectively pulls monsters into range for faster takedowns.

Gathers sand around yourself, dealing a burst of Attack DMG to surrounding enemies. The sand then solidifies, dealing Attack DMG to surrounding enemies every second for 6s . Throughout this effect, continuously regenerates Rage and Sand Crystal , providing 33 Rage and 6 Sand Crystals . Tips: Keep it active as often as possible. The continuous AoE DMG poses a great threat to the enemies while generating Rage quickly.

Creates a rocky barrier around yourself, automatically countering Lethal Skills for a period of time and increasing Block DMG Reduction . Each Sand Crystal consumed extends the duration by 1s (up to 5s ). Tips: Time carefully and use it during massive incoming Attack DMG to maximize Block DMG Reduction and minimize DMG taken.
Consumes Sand Crystals and Rage , dealing Attack DMG to the target and reducing DMG taken for the next 10s (non-stackable).

Consumes 50 Rage and 5 Sand Crystals to unleash a roar, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies and granting a Shield that absorbs all damage (stacks up to 50% of Max HP). Also reduces Attack DMG taken by 10% for 12 seconds. Tips: Provides output capabilities when survival pressure is minimal and grants greater Attack DMG Reduction under conditions where enemy units predominantly inflict Attack DMG.

Empowered ​Granite Fury​ channels the Power of Rock to summon a massive boulder from above, dealing Attack DMG equal to 800% ATK to the enemies within range (which scales with the Level/Tier of ​Granite Fury​ ) and always triggering Crit.

Consumes 50 Rage and 5 Sand Crystals to unleash a roar, dealing Attack DMG to nearby enemies and granting a Shield that absorbs all damage (stacks up to 150% of Max HP). Also reduces Attack DMG taken by 10% for 12 seconds. Tips: Provides output capabilities when survival pressure is minimal and grants greater armor under conditions where enemy units predominantly inflict Attack DMG.
Enters Focus state, greatly increasing Haste and reducing the CD of Special Attacks by 50% . Tips: Best paired with Falconry Spec. Use it just before activating Photon Reforge for maximum uptime.

Charges and then fires a piercing arrow that deals Attack DMG and Knockback to all enemies in its path. Cannot knock back targets with Resilience, but reduces targets' Resilience. Powerdraw deals a bonus 100% Crit DMG. This skill holds 2 charges. No charge time required when in Photon Reforge state. Tips: Great for reducing enemies' Resilience while dealing area damage.

Charges and fires Photon Arrows to a target area, dealing continuous Attack DMG . The damage interval scales with Attack SPD. While in Photon Reforge state, Photon Arrows consume no Photon Energy, generate extra arrows, and deal 50% more Attack DMG . Tips: Casting during Photon Reforge increases its damage and consumes no Photon Energy.

Leaps upward swiftly and fires at enemies, dealing Attack DMG . Grants immunity to Attack DMG for you and up to 10 nearby Allies for 5s . This skill holds 2 charges. Tips: This is intended to be equipped in high-pressure situations to increase survivability.

Summons a powerful combat Companion to provide assistance in battle. Summon Wild Wolf : The summoned Wild Wolf pounces on the current target, dealing Attack DMG to the target and nearby enemies, then joins the battle for 20s before disappearing. Summon Falcon : The summoned Falcon dives in a straight line, dealing Attack DMG to all enemies in its path before disappearing. Tips: Boosts the number of active Companions during the battle. Casting is recommended when all buffs are prepared to ensure maximum efficiency.

Fires an Explosive Arrow at the target that detonates on impact. The Explosive Arrow deals Attack DMG to all nearby enemies. Each time when a Class Skill deals Crit DMG, Explosive Arrow gains 1 charge. At 5 charges or after 6s , the Explosive Arrow explodes, each charge increases the DMG of Explosive Arrow by 100% . Tips: Better paired with Falconry Spec. Focus on Crit DMG to power up the explosion.

Consumes 3 Performance Passion to swing your guitar with force, dealing heavy Magic DMG to enemies. Performance Passion : Required to perform music. Regenerates 1 stack every 5s . Tips: High coverage healing skill. Use it before your Performance Passion overflows.

Consumes 3 stacks of Performance Passion to play a tune that heals the caster and the nearby ally with the lowest HP (party members prioritized). The healing amount scales with the caster's MATK (plus an additional fixed heal equal to 3% of the target's Max HP). Performance Passion : Required to perform music. 1 point is regenerated every 5s . Tips: A healing skill with high uptime. Cast it to avoid letting Performance Passion overflow.

My Passion Still Burns! Consumes 5 stacks of Performance Passion to summon a randomly shaped graffiti on the ground, healing 10 allies (party members prioritized) and dealing Magic DMG to the enemies within range. While standing within the graffiti, the caster gains 10% Fire Bonus. Only 1 graffiti can exist at a time. Performance Passion : Required to perform music. 1 point is regenerated every 5s . Tips: This skill has the widest range for both healing and DMG. Cast it once the CD ends for max effectiveness.

A rousing melody. When Performance Energy exceeds 15 stacks, you can begin the performance, which cannot be stopped once started. CD: 5s . While performing Heroic Melody , you consume 6 Performance Energy per second, and every 3s , 10 allies restore HP (Interval affected by Haste). While you perform Heroic Melody , every 7s , your String Strike transforms into Fierce Strike . While you perform Heroic Melody , the conversion rate of Peaceful Tune + 50% . Performance Energy : Required to play Melody skills ( Heroic Melody and Healing Melody ). 1 point of energy is regenerated per second. Tips: The skill can't be stopped manually, so time its activation wisely to maximize synergy with Peaceful Tune and Fierce Strike.

Let the passion surge again! Consumes 3 Performance Passion , reigniting the spirits of the weary. Performs a sequence of notes that restores HP to 10 allies within range (prioritizing teammates) and grants Tenacity Chord. Each stack of Tenacity Chord additionally increases Max HP by 0.5% (up to 2.5% Max HP) for 5 s (duration cannot be refreshed once 5 stacks are reached). Performance Passion : Required to perform music. Regenerates 1 stack every 5s . Tips: Highest healing potential. Monitor your team's health to maximize efficiency and prevent overhealing.

Strums the strings and releases searing flames forward, dealing Magic DMG to the enemies within range. Charging alters the skill's range and DMG. Tier 1 : Chants for 0.7s , targeting a fan-shaped area with an 8 -meter radius in front. Tier 2 : Chants for 1.4s , targeting a fan-shaped area with an 8 -meter radius in front and increasing DMG by 50% . Tier 3 : Chants for 2.1s , targeting a fan-shaped area with an 8 -meter radius in front and increasing DMG by 100% . Tips: High DMG skill. Combine with Talent effects and the amplifier for strong DMG and healing. Be mindful of environmental safety during casting.

As a passionate music lover, your impromptu performance immediately grants 5 Performance Passion . It also heals nearby allies and gives them a Shield that lasts for 10 s, while dealing Magic DMG to nearby enemies. Performance Passion : Required to perform music. Regenerates 1 stack every 5 s. Tips: In emergencies, this powerful shield can ease the team's survival pressure. Time the cast carefully.

The perfect piece for fan interaction. Grants Encore effect to 10 allies for 10s . Encore : Grants Super Armor . Each time an offensive or healing Expertise Skill is cast, there is a 50% fixed chance to trigger Encore Strings once, dealing DMG to the current target or healing the lowest-HP ally. Tips: Cast during your team's burst window for optimal DMG and healing of Encore.

Channels for 6s and continuously spews searing flames forward, dealing Magic DMG equal to 1000% ATK in total to the enemies within range. Tips: Move continuously and try to maximize DMG dealt while staying safe.

Instantly releases a powerful sonic wave, dealing Magic DMG to nearby enemies. Heals nearby allies and grants a Shield that lasts for 10 s. Doubles the Performance Passion cap and fully restores Performance Passion . Performance Passion : Required to perform music. Regenerates 1 stack every 5 s. Tips: A powerful emergency shield to ease team survival pressure. Time the cast carefully. Once fully charged with Performance Passion, trigger burst.

Consumes 1 Holy Sigil to deliver a powerful shield bash to enemies in front, dealing Attack DMG and increasing your Armor, stacking up to 3 times. Tips: Monitor the Armor buff from Valor Bash and try to keep it active at all times.

Consumes 1 Holy Sigil . After a brief charge, performs a fierce sweep forward, dealing Attack DMG and gaining 2 stacks of Lightforged Barrier . Lightforged Barrier : Each stack increases max HP by 2% , up to 10 stacks. Taking any DMG consumes 1 stack. The Barrier lasts 25s or until all stacks are consumed. Gaining a new stack refreshes the duration. Tips: Maintain high stacks of Lightforged Barrier while weaving in attacks. Pay attention to the use of Vanguard Hunt to trigger bonus effects.

Unleashes holy energy to strike nearby enemies, dealing Attack DMG and inflicting Dazzle for 5s . Grants a Radiant Shield equal to 300% ATK. For the next 10s , instantly refreshes 1 Holy Sigil for every 2s (prioritizing the Holy Sigil with the longest remaining CD), and generates 10 Photon Energy each time. Radiant Shield : Infuses the Shield with light, absorbing 50% of incoming DMG. The effect can stack absorption and reset duration when the Skill is reused. Max absorption cannot exceed 100% of Max HP. Tips: Instantly boosts survivability and generates Holy Sigil and Photon Energy. Time the casts wisely.

Consumes up to 8 stacks of Lightforged Barrier , summoning continuous radiant energy to spiral rapidly around you. Each second, it deals Attack DMG to nearby enemies (interval affected by Attack Speed) and grants 1 stack of Lightforged Barrier . Each time it deals DMG to 1 target, restores 1% max HP (up to 5% ). When activated, each stack of Lightforged Barrier adds 2s to the duration, up to a maximum of 16s . Lightforged Barrier : Max HP + 2% with each stack. Lightforged Barrier stacks up to 10 times. Any incoming DMG consumes 1 stack. The effect lasts 25s or until all stacks are consumed. Duration resets each time a new stack is gained. Tips: Cast Lightforged Barrier to deal DMG and heal. Cast the skill when Lightforged Barrier is fully stacked to achieve excellent defense and burst potential.

Gains unwavering resolve and throws 5 shields at the enemies within 10m (closest first), dealing Attack DMG and interrupting them. Afterward, throws 1 time every 2s and gains 10 Photon Energy each time. For the next 10s , each instance of damage taken is reduced by a percentage of the caster's Max HP, and the caster automatically counters Lethal Skill . Tips: This skill requires no Photon Energy or Holy Sigil to cast and provides solid survivability, making it suitable as an opener.

Consumes 3 Holy Sigils , summoning a sword from beneath the target's feet to deal Attack DMG to the target, while gaining 5 stacks of Lightforged Barrier . Lightforged Barrier : Each stack increases the final Max HP by 2% . You can have up to 10 stacks of Lightforged Barrier, and any damage taken will consume 1 stack. It lasts for 25s or until all stacks are consumed, and the duration resets each time a stack is gained. Tips: While having considerable damage capability, it can efficiently replenish Lightforged Barrier.
Shield Toss consumes Photon Energy to hurl a spinning shield, dealing Attack DMG to enemies it hits, interrupting them and reducing all damage they deal to the caster for a duration.
Gathers surrounding energy to pull all enemies within 30 meters to you, inflicting taunt . Gain DMG Reduction for a period of time. Passive Effect: Thorn .
Grants 45% additional DMG Reduction and Super Armor for 10s . This skill is unaffected by CD effects .
Conceals the caster's presence to prevent Aggro generation and cleanses all debuffs from the caster for 10s . This skill is unaffected by CD effects .
Raises a Block Shield for 2s . The Block Shield will block the next incoming hit. Successful Block reduces the CD of all your Weapon skills.

Slam the ground 5 meters in front of you, creating a powerful tremor that stuns all enemies within range. If the enemy has Super Armor , this will instead deal significant Super Armor damage. If you successfully evade Lethal Skill , CD will be reset immediately.
Releases an energy wave, interrupting all targets within 5m and silencing them for 5s . This skill is unaffected by CD effects .
Revives the nearest ally within 3m . This skill is unaffected by CD effects . Weakness: Unaffected by same type of effects for 60s (Weakness effects are enhanced in party dungeons in Nightmare mode).

Immediately grants the caster and up to 10 nearby allies (party members prioritized) a shield equal to 20% Max HP, and while the shield persists, increases 15% additional DMG Reduction for 10s . This skill is unaffected by CD effects .
Raises a Block Shield for 2s . The Block Shield will block the next incoming hit. Successful Block reduces the CD of all your Weapon skills.

Channels the power of the stars, entering Star Calling state. While active, greatly increases your Sigil chance and grants Sigil: Falling Star . Sigil : When DMG is dealt, there is chance to summon 1 meteor to bombard the target area, dealing area damage. More meteors are summoned based on your Sigil chance . This effect has a CD, which - your Sigil chance .

Focuses on your Energy and enter Charge state. While active, Consecutive Hits and Defeats generate up to 5 Engram Orbs. When the duration ends or the skill is cast again, deals DMG based on the number of orbs stored. For every 8 hits, 1 Engram Orb is generated. For every Defeat, 1 Engram Orb is generated. Area damage that hits multiple targets is still counted as a single hit.
Grants 35% additional DMG Reduction for 5s . This skill can store 2 charges. This skill is unaffected by CD effects .
Instantly recovers 50% Stamina and increases Movement Speed by 15% for 5s . This skill is unaffected by CD effects .

Leaps into the air for a powerful strike. If the attack lands a Crit , the CD of this skill will be reset, and it can be cast up to 5 times in succession. Each cast temporarily increases Crit DMG , stacking up to 5 times.

Unleashes Sigil: Blazing Surge , dealing minor area damage and creating Blazing Traps in the area. These traps explode on contact with enemies or after a period of time, dealing DMG to surrounding enemies . Sigil : Summon at least 2 Blazing Traps, with a chance to summon up to 5 .

Transforms into Boss: Inferno Ogre to unleash a forward fiery breath that deals Attack DMG and interrupts affected targets. Concurrently, applies Healing to you, and 100% excess healing is converted into a Shield lasting 20s . The transformed form reduces DMG taken by 50% .
Summons Boss : Tempest Ogre and channels the power of thunder to generate a vortex, continuously pulling in enemies near the target and dealing AoE Magic DMG when the duration ends.

Transforms into Boss : Brigand Leader and summons a blazing giant axe, increasing the party's ATK within range for a period and granting yourself additional ATK boost. (This effect cannot stack and only one can be active at a time.)

Summons Elite : Boarrier Tyrant to charge forward with tusks for 3s . Deals Attack DMG and knocks enemies airborne during the charge. Transforms into Elite : Inferno Goblin Mage and summons meteors from the sky, dealing Magic DMG and interrupting the target's actions. Upon the skill cast, your Intellect is increased for a period.
[Elite Summon] - Void Foxen. Pounces forward with blinding speed, dealing AoE Attack DMG and increasing Haste for 20s .

Summons Elite : Void Ogre, roars in place, and fires 6 whirlwind-like Void Projectiles at the target, dealing Attack DMG . Inflicts Void Corruption Decay on the target for 10s , dealing Magic DMG per second, up to 5 stacks. 100% of the DMG dealt over time is converted into your HP.

Summons Elite : Goblin Guard to perform multiple sword energy attacks forward, dealing Attack DMG . Sword energy hits will reduce the target's Armor . (The effect cannot stack, and only one effect of the same type will be effective.) Upon the skill cast, your Block DMG reduction is increased for a period.
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 1
[Boss Summon] - Crimson Foxen. Strike instantly, dealing 1 instance of Attack DMG . Then it continues assisting the player in combat for 15s . Can be directed via Storm Arrow from the Marksman.

Summons Olvera to shuttle back and forth in a forward direction, drawing in enemies encountered along the path, dealing Attack DMG , and interrupting their actions. When dealing DMG, there is a chance to inflict Seed of Lightning on the targets for 10s . Dealing DMG to targets with Seed of Lightning will cause an explosion (CD: 2s ), dealing Magic DMG . Any target with Seed of Lightning defeated will reduce CD time by 20s .
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 2

Transforms into Elite : Mighty Colossus to charge and deal Attack DMG . The longer you charge, the greater the effect on Resilience breaking. Each stack increases the Resilience Break done by 50% . ( 3 stacks at Tier 3 and 6 stacks at Tier 5.) Upon the skill cast, your Resilience Break Bonus is increased for a period.
Summons Elite : Muku Scout to chase the target, dealing Attack DMG . Upon the skill cast, immediately gains full passive effects, and the stack count is doubled within 20s .
Transforms into Elite : Void Arachnocrab, and gains Invincibility for 5s .

[Boss Summon] - Dogorman. Transforms into Boss Dogorman and let out a roar, summoning a sandstone field that follows you for 10s . Grants DMG Reduction to allies in the field. [Non-stackable. Only one effect of the same type may be active]
Resonates with the power of Elite: Crimson Sprayer to transform into its form. Deals Attack DMG to nearby enemies and inflicts 100% Wound for 15s .
[Elite Summon] - Axe Muku. Deals Attack DMG , reducing the target's ATK for 10s . [Non-stackable. Only one effect of the same type may be active]
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 3

Transforms into Boss : Golden Juggernaut, granting yourself and 10 allies Shield . When dealing DMG, the shielded targets generate Thunderstrike (CD: 0.5s ), and the DMG dealt depends on the friendly ATK. (This effect cannot stack and only one will be effective.)

Summons Boss : Venobzzar Incubator to continuously attack surrounding units, dealing Attack DMG . Each attack inflicts Vulnerability on the target, and your DMG dealt to the target is increased. (This effect cannot stack and only one will be effective.)
Summons Boss : Iron Fang to deliver AoE Attack DMG to nearby enemies, inflicting a 100% Wound on all affected targets for 15s .
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 4
Summons Boss : Lizardman King to deal Ice Attack DMG to nearby enemies and Silence them for 10s .

Resonates with the power of Boss: Goblin King, summoning 1–3 goblins at random to cast skills. Always summons 1 from Elite: Goblin Guard or Elite: Goblin Warrior. Has a chance to additionally summon 1 Elite: Jungle Goblin Warrior. Has a chance to summon 1 from Elite: Storm Goblin Axe or Boss: Storm Goblin King. Has a 30% chance to summon the Boss.

Summons Rorola, resonating with the power of ancestors to gain a damage boost for some time. Also, every 10 hits on targets grant an additional damage boost, stacking up to 5 times . Once the cap is reached, subsequent hits extend the duration of the additional boost (the duration of the Base DMG boost does not extend). Each extension adds 3 s, with a maximum of 5 extensions. At the same time, grants the Life Steal effect, restoring HP equal to a portion of damage dealt (the duration can extend). This skill holds 2 charges.

Transforms into Dorothy, replacing basic attack modules and gaining Artisan's Power . Passive: Dealing damage has a 40% chance to trigger Chain Lightning (trigger interval: at least 0.5s ). ① Charges and fires a powerful shot at the target, dealing Attack DMG . Each additional charge increases the damage by 150% . ② Leaps into the air and launches a Thunderstorm Bolt at the target, dealing Attack DMG and creating a Thunderstorm Zone at the target for 7s. Thunderstorm Zone deals Attack DMG per second to enemies within and slows them. ③ Continuously unleashes Thunder Tracers, dealing Attack DMG and inflicting Paralysis on hit. ④ Fires an Oblivion Bomb, which explodes after traveling a distance or upon impact, dealing Attack DMG .

Summons Boyce to create a field of frost by concentrating ice power, dealing Ice Magic DMG . After casting, your ATK is increased for a period of time. Each cast of a Special Attack grants an additional increase, stacking up to 5 times. At max stacks, gain a bonus to Attack SPD and Casting SPD . Performing a Special Attack extends this bonus's duration by 3s , up to a max of 5 times (The ATK bonus's duration is not affected). This skill holds 2 charges.

Summons Fafala to create a field. You and allies within the field gain Final DMG Reduction and Super Armor . When you deal damage from inside the field, inflict bonus damage based on a percentage of your DEF (can trigger at most once every 1s ). When you take damage, reduce the CD of this Skill by 1s (can trigger at most once every 2s ). [This effect does not stack. Only one instance of this effect can be active at a time.

Summons Boss: Goblin Chief to briefly charge up and unleash a forward blade wave that deals Attack DMG . After casting, your Expertise Skill's DMG and healing are increased for a period of time. During this time, dealing damage with an Expertise Skill reduces the CD of this Skill by 0.3s (can trigger at most once every 1s ).
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 5

Summons Boss: Cabbage Kingpin to briefly charge up and slam the ground with a hammer, dealing Attack DMG . After casting, your passive effect is locked to the displayed sigil for 20s , and its effect is increased by 100%-150% .

Summons Boss: Flamehorn to repeatedly ram the target with its horns, dealing Attack DMG . Grants a Luck effect: Triggering a Lucky Strike causes an explosion at the target's location, dealing Magic DMG (cooldown: 0.1s ), and immediately grants the Absolute Luck effect. For the duration, Absolute Luck's cooldown becomes 5s .

Summons Elite: Blackstone Commander to call down lightning from the sky, dealing Magic DMG . For a period of time after the skill is cast, when you deal damage, you will also deal additional Attack DMG to the target equal to a percentage of your Armor (can trigger at most once every 1s ).

Transforms into Elite: Blackstone Vanguard to perform a spinning attack that deals Fire Attack DMG . Every stack of Blade Intent allows for an additional spin (up to 15 stacks). This damage benefits from all types of elemental bonuses and is not affected by passive effects.
Summons Elite: Goblin Trickster to channel for a long time before dealing massive AoE Magic DMG . (This skill damages enemies and up to 20 allies!)

Summons Elite: Goblin Shaman to briefly channel before summoning an exploding magic orb. The explosion deals Magic DMG to targets in the area and heals up to 10 nearby allies (prioritizing teammates). After casting, for 20s , you deal damage every 2s to the surrounding area equal to 50% of the self-healing from your Class Skills.
Skill Effect Enhancement, Tier 6

Summons Denvel to attract nearby monsters and deal Attack DMG . After casting, grants a temporary enhancement: the user takes damage equal to 0.1% of Max HP every 0.2s and gains a DMG boost, with an additional boost for every 100,000 Max HP (Total base and extra DMG boost is capped, and the Max HP requirement is adjusted each season). This skill holds 2 charges.

Summons Plague Nappo. The Nappo's attack method and skill effects change based on the type of skill cast previously. If cast directly or after a Special Attack , summons Stormblade Nappo to deal AoE Attack DMG once, and reduces the current Resonance Skill's CD by 81.25% . If cast after an Expertise Skill , summons Marksman Nappo to deal Attack DMG to a single target, and reduces the current Resonance Skill's CD by 68.75% . If cast after an Ultimate , summons Wind Knight Nappo to deal Attack DMG once, reduces the current Resonance Skill's CD by 25% , and temporarily increases your DMG . If cast after another Resonance Skill , summons Beat Performer Nappo to reduce the CD of the previously cast Resonance Skill (excluding this one).

Summons Boss: Predator Spider to deal Attack DMG . After casting, your passive ATK bonus is temporarily enhanced according to your Mastery Percentage . Every 5% Mastery grants extra ATK for each passive stack (up to a max limit).
Summons Boss: Rebel King to deal Attack DMG . After casting, temporarily grants full passive stacks, with the effect multiplied by 2 .

Summons Boss: Void Watcher, dealing Magic DMG and occupying an area for a period of time. You and your teammates within the area gain increased ATK , Attack SPD , and Casting SPD . The effect on yourself is multiplied by 2.5 . (Does not stack; only one of the same effect may be active.)

Summons Boss: Bloodthirsty Furball to deal Attack DMG . For a period of time after casting, every time your Class Skills and Luck effect deal damage, they add extra damage on top of the skill's base value, equal to a certain percentage of your ATK.
Summons Elite: Killer Arachnocrab to deal Attack DMG . After casting, you gain full passive stacks for a period of time, during which they do not decrease.

Transform into Celestial Spirit Mage - Lucy, replacing your skill set while gaining Ability Conversion . Fleuve d'Étoiles : Manifests the Fleuve d'Étoiles and swings it continuously, dealing Light Magic DMG to targets. 2. Celestial Guardian : Harnesses the power of Celestial Spirits to grant a shield lasting 20s to up to 10 allies within range (prioritizing teammates). Simultaneously inflicts debuffs on up to 5 enemies within range, reducing ATK, applying Vulnerability, and reducing Element Resistance for 10s . 3. Aqua Metria : Draws upon the power of Aquarius to unleash waves forward, dealing Water Magic DMG to targets in their path, with an additional 50% of the damage dealt converted into healing.

Fire Dragon's Iron Fist : Charges briefly before unleashing a blazing punch forward, dealing Fire Attack DMG and accumulating 5 stacks of Dragon Flame . 2. Fire Dragon's Roar : Gathers the power of flames to spew a massive blast of fire forward, dealing Fire Attack DMG . If at max Dragon Force stacks, consumes all stacks of Dragon Force to gain CD reduction for Natsu's skills and a Fire Bonus.
