There are two Life Skills: Gathering and Crafting . Crafting lets you use materials gathered through Gathering to create a wide variety of useful items. With Life Skills, adventurers can craft items for sale at the Trading Center to earn Luno, or produce their own gear, furniture, and more. Gathering and Crafting actions come in two types: Focused and Regular. Performing a Focused Action consumes Focus , while a Regular Action costs nothing. Focused Actions are usually unlocked by learning a Mastery . Every 300 Focus consumed earns you 1 Mastery point. Mastery points are shared across all Life Skills. If you're unhappy with your chosen Mastery, you can reset them individually per Class. Regular Actions are typically unlocked by increasing your Life Skill Level . Weekly Supply Quests are a major source of Life Skills EXP. Each Focused or Crafting Action grants a large amount of EXP. Even Regular Actions will grant a certain amount of EXP. There are no limits on how many Life Skills you can unlock. Adventurers are free to unlock them all. Unlocking any Life Skill for the first time grants 3 Mastery points and 2 Mastery Reset Tickets. Need a certain Life Skill material in a hurry? Try visiting the Exchange Store of each Class's instructor.

Focused : You can create items such as Mystery Metal and Radiant Stone, which may be traded at the Trading Center or used personally. The materials required for crafting these items are primarily sourced from Mineralogy and Artisanry . Regular : You can create non-tradable items such as certain weapons, heavy armor, homestead construction materials, and metal furniture. The materials required for crafting these items are primarily gathered through Mineralogy , or further processed via Smelting, Gemcrafting, and Alchemy .

Protect Tina: The Kanamia souls from Tina's memories drain her sanity. Defeat the monsters as quickly as possible. Tips: Focus on eliminating monsters with Void Engram first, as they inflict the greatest sanity loss on Tina.

Sky Crack: Kartgriff charges an Electromagnetic Core and summons charging lasers to empower it. If the laser hits the core, it triggers massive DMG across the whole battlefield. If it hits a player, it stacks Electromagnetic Vulnerability, increasing the DMG they take. Tips: Players should take turns intercepting the laser to prevent it from hitting the core. Healers must restore intercepted players' HP. On Hard mode and above, an electromagnetic zone continuously Opens at the center-dodge accordingly.

Soul Pool Ritual: Maximo and his two partners summon soul weapons and pray for the Soul Pool's blessing. During this time, the Soul Pool fires continuous soul barrages at players. Players must defeat all three soul weapons. Tips: Split your team to attack all soul weapons. Coordinate DMG output to keep their HP balanced and defeat them around the same time to prevent regeneration.

Military Formation: Goblins are summoned to form battle lines. After a few seconds, they charge at players. Among them, two Goblin Swordmen carry Wind Shields, which drop upon defeat. Tips: Look for the goblins with Wind Shields and take them down separately. Then, stand in the gaps of the charging formation to avoid taking DMG. On Hard mode and above, goblins charge in double rows. Watch carefully for safe spots to dodge the charge.

Spark of the Storm: Shuro Barot summons a Storm Domain and condenses a Storm Core, launching it toward players. Players holding a Wind Shield can tap the extra skill button to deflect the core. If the Storm Core hits Shuro Barot, it interrupts his casting. If it hits the Storm Domain, it triggers area damage across the whole battlefield. Tips: Stand in the Storm Core's path early to deflect it. Multiple players can work together to coordinate the bounces. On Hard mode and above, Shuro Barot also summons a Storm Barrier-players must bounce the core multiple times to let it bypass the barrier.

Wind Spirit Summon: Igoreus summons Wind Spirits and later absorbs them to enhance himself. Killing Wind Spirits generates Wind Spirit Energy. Players who collect this energy will gain increased ATK but reduced defense. Tips: Quickly kill Wind Spirits after they spawn. On Hard Mode, their death deals massive DMG to the players, so take turns to kill them promptly. Plan how many energy pickups each player gets to avoid severe defense loss.

Lightning Storm: Igoreus absorbs all Wind Spirits and Wind Spirit Energy on the field to form a shield and begins a wide-range lightning bombardment. Breaking the shield will interrupt the cast and render Igoreus Vulnerable. The faster the shield is broken, the longer the Vulnerable duration. Tips: Save burst skills for quickly breaking the shield. Leave Wind Spirit Energy on the field and collect it right before this skill for more ATK.

Howling Gale: Igoreus summons strong horizontal winds and flies into the storm, searching for a chance to sweep across the field from above, dealing massive DMG to players on half of the field. Tips: Push against the wind and watch the enemy's position. Igoreus's wings glow on the side he will swoop from.

Void Corruption Infliction: Within the Dark Mist Fortress, players are continuously afflicted by Void Corruption. As Void Corruption accumulates, reaching 100 stacks will result in loss of sanity and death. Tips: Players with high Void Corruption should group up at the gravity device to purge the Void Corruption.
Void Corruption: Inside the Dark Mist Fortress, players are continuously affected by Void Corruption, accumulating Void Corruption stacks. Upon reaching 100 stacks, players will lose sanity and die.

Dagger of Execution: The Shadow Bladedancer targets a player and summons Dagger of Execution that strikes after a delay, executing the target and dealing DMG in a small area. The marked player must use the Soul Totem to gain Life Shelter to survive. Tips: Marked players must reach a Soul Totem quickly.
Gate of Wraith: Wraiths emerge and move toward Shadow Bladedancer, who absorbs them to recover HP and boosts ATK. Tips: Focus down the wraiths immediately.

Undead Revival: The Shadow Bladedancer summons Lost Wraiths. Players must touch and escort each wraith to a Soul Totem to purify it. When the timer expires, DMG is dealt based on the number of wraiths purified. Tips: Avoid crossing teammates' escort paths. Otherwise, the wraith falls back to Lost state.

Shackles of Souls: The Shadow Bladedancer binds the soul of a targeted player and summons a Dagger of Execution that descends slowly. Failure to break the chain in time results in massive decay DMG. Tips: Beware of detonating Wraith Totems near teammates.

Haunting Nightmare: Tethers multiple players, dealing DMG over time and inflicting stackable Healing Reduction. Players can move apart to break the tether, but it triggers a large explosion and inflicts Neverending Nightmares on all players. While this effect lasts, any subsequent tether break deals massively increased explosion DMG. Tips: Break tethers one by one after the previous player's vulnerability ends.
Akufis feeds on subterranean crystals and strengthens itself as it absorbs them. Tips: Once Akufis absorbs enough crystal, it summons Serpent Eggs to aid it.

Hide-and-Seek: Plague Nappo creates multiple clones and transforms both clones and players into hide-and-seek objects around the field. At the end of the skill duration, Plague Nappo will attack all adventurers standing in the wrong positions, and its clones will also appear to attack adventurers. Tips: Adventurers must ensure that objects in the scene (adventurers and clones) are placed in the correct positions: Follow the prompt to check the field objects and find the position you should be in (your ground marker turns green at the correct position). Defeat the incorrectly positioned Plague Nappo clones at the same time.

Lightless Realm: The Light Devourer covers the field in darkness. Adventurers lose HP continuously in the darkness, and the damage dealt is greatly reduced. Tips: Adventurers must avoid staying in the darkness. Seek a Light Domain to dispel the darkness, fighting the boss within the Light Domain.

Dark Pulse: The Light Devourer will lock on the Light Domain and, after a delay, repeatedly unleash Dark Pulse, greatly draining its Light Energy. If Dark Rifts are present, they also mimic the Light Devourer, locking on the Light Domain and unleashing Dark Pulse. Tips: A damage warning zone appears when the Light Devourer unleashes Dark Pulse. An adventurer must quickly pick up the Light Domain and reposition it to safety before Dark Pulse hits. When moving the Light Domain, always watch teammate positions to avoid plunging them into darkness.

Frenzied Darkness: The Light Devourer enters a special state, gains a shield, and continuously casts skills, dealing damage to all adventurers until the shield is broken. Tips: Monitor the Light Devourer's skill timing and keep your burst skills ready. Once the shield comes up, fire off burst and shatter it as quickly as possible.

Malice Combo: The Purifier teleports to the field and marks its current aggro target. After a delay, it will charge that adventurer. Once the charge ends, the Purifier immediately marks two adventurers. After a delay, bombardments fall on the marked players. Tips: Everyone must stack together to share the damage when the boss charges. Afterward, the players marked for bombardment must immediately enter a Stasis Zone to mitigate the damage.

Purification Burst: The Purifier marks several adventurers with Purification Energy. It explodes after a delay, dealing heavy damage to the target's current plane. Tips: Place some Pulse Fountains inside Stasis Zones in advance to slow down the Pulse Fountains. When Purification Energy is about to explode, use the fountains to reach different heights, preventing multiple Purification Energies from detonating on the same height level.

Matrix Protocol: Matrix Towers are summoned into the field in batches. Once a Matrix Tower's progress bar is full, its charging is complete. When three fully charged blue Matrix Towers are connected in a line, the team-wiping Divine Retribution Protocol is triggered. Tips: Carefully guide the Disintegration Beam to convert blue Matrix Towers into gold ones. When three golden Matrix Towers are connected in a line, the boss will be forced into a Protocol Collapse state.

Polarized Judgment: Three heavy-duty tripod robots appear on the field. An Ion Blade randomly spawns on either the left or right side of each robot. After a few seconds, they charge forward, dealing massive AoE damage to the side of the field corresponding to the Ion Blade. Tips: Identify the position of the robots' Ion Blades to determine which side is the safe zone. The overlapping safe zone of all three robots is where players can avoid damage. Move there promptly to dodge the attack.

Matrix Towers: Matrix Towers that appear on the field initially exist in an ethereal form while slowly accumulating a progress bar. After 40s, they materialize into physical Matrix Towers, indicating that charging is complete. At that moment, they will deal AoE damage. Tips: Two Matrix Towers will complete charging simultaneously. Pay attention to positioning and avoid standing at the intersection of the two large AoE damage zones.

Overheated: In the Uncontrolled Roar state, Thanatos - Final Form gains an ATK boost. When Thanatos - Final Form enters steam, it will continuously release thermal shocks before entering a CD state, removing one stack of the ATK boost. Tips: Monitor Thanatos - Final Form's ATK boost stacks and lure it into the steam at the right time.

Overdrive Bombardment: Thanatos - Final Form enters a charging state and launches an artillery strike after a period of time. Use the cannons in the arena to defeat Thanatos - Final Form. Tips: Destroy the charging turrets and guide them to a designated location. Turrets will prioritize following healers within their range. When the monsters summoned by Thanatos - Final Form are defeated, they drop electrical energy. Use the energy to charge available cannons to fight against Thanatos - Final Form.

Void Corruption Curse: Void Tina deals damage to the entire arena and curses several cabinets. The cursed cabinets will erupt with Void Corruption after a period of time. Tips: Interact with a cabinet before it erupts to absorb the Void Corruption. After absorbing it, allow it to detonate in a safe location.

Void Corruption Oppression: After charging for a period of time, Void Tina attacks the entire arena. Tina (Original Form) blesses several cabinets. Quickly move to the vicinity of the blessed cabinets to avoid the damage. Tips: Move near the blessed cabinets to take cover before the charging finishes. On Hard Mode or above, this skill disables Phantom Dash, so make use of the teleportation mechanic between cabinets wisely.

Void Corruption Strike: After charging for a period of time, Void Tina sequentially attacks targets on the field in numerical order, dealing massive damage. On Master difficulty or above, each attack is followed by an extra super-wide slash to the right. Tips: Spread out to prevent taking multiple hits. On Master difficulty or above, be careful not to stand to the right of other players to avoid taking secondary damage.

Void Corruption Clone: Summons a clone at the edge of the arena. After a brief delay, the clone unleashes a continuously advancing wave of Void Corruption toward the center of the arena. Tips: Observe the clone's position, move to the cabinet opposite the clone in advance, and teleport to the other side at the right moment to avoid the damage.

Scar: Mist-Piercing Fang uses its sharp claws, fangs, and compressed airflow to deal heavy Bleed damage to adventurers, deplete their Armor, and disable healing skills. Tips: Adventurers must proactively take on the various debuffs applied by Mist-Piercing Fang according to their roles.

Opportunistic Pounce: The boss randomly targets an adventurer without the Scar debuff, deals damage and applies a Red Scar. Tips: Adventurers on the field should maintain a Scar debuff that does not interfere with their role's functionality.

Mighty Bite: Mist-Piercing Fang uses wind magic to root its current aggro target and leaps backward. It then targets the nearest adventurer in front of it, deals damage, and applies a Blue Scar. Tips: Non-Guardian adventurers must stand in front of Mist-Piercing Fang to prevent Guardian adventurers from having their armor broken.

Call Windblade: Mist-Piercing Fang teleports to the center of the arena and summons a Windblade Orb that flies toward itself. Upon contact with the orb, Mist-Piercing Fang immediately unseals its power, gaining a massive ATK boost. Tip: Adventurers should position themselves at intervals along the Windblade Orb's path to gradually weaken it as it flies.

Seed of Imprisonment: The Illusory Bloom Cocoon randomly spawns four blooming Illusory Blooms around itself. The Illusory Blooms last for 30s, and touching them inflicts a root effect. In Master Mode, naturally dissipating Illusory Blooms will leave behind a Corruption Zone. Tips: During non-essential mechanic phases in combat, split up to step on the Illusory Blooms and purify them. Purify them promptly to avoid impacting core mechanics.

Sky Crack - Reverse: Kartgriff charges an Electromagnetic Core and summons charging lasers to empower it. If a laser hits the core, it gains charge. Charging reduces Corruption and Kartgriff's HP in the Lunalusion dimension. Lasers hitting players deal damage; in Master Mode, they also apply Electromagnetic Vulnerability stacks. Illusory Bloom Cocoons attempt to interfere with the charging by constantly summoning Illusory Blooms in the arena. Lasers hitting an Illusory Bloom destroy it, dealing AoE damage and stacking Corruption. Tips: Block the laser path appropriately to clear the Illusory Blooms on one side, then allow the laser on the other side to fully charge the core.

Dimensional Banishment - Reverse: Players return to the real dimension by breaking the Illusory Blooms. Monsters corrupted by the Illusory Blooms continuously unleash AoE damage to prevent Kartgriff's recovery. Tips: DPS players should break the enemy monsters' toughness gauges, while healers should take the opportunity to continuously heal allied monsters. Pick up Engram Orbs to suppress Corruption.

Momentary Rift: Players return to the real dimension by breaking the Illusory Blooms. In the real dimension, there are four portals, categorized as either real or Lunalusion. The Lunalusion portals visible to each player differ, and only the overlapping portals are the correct ones. During this period, Corruption continuously increases, and players constantly take damage. Tips: First, gather at one portal and observe the number of players, then move to another. The portal with the most players is the correct one.

Cold Wave Symphony: Summons stack markers of different elements. After a brief delay, bubble attacks of the corresponding elements descend. If no players are inside a stack marker, a second, arena-wide attack is triggered. Tips: Split into two groups to share the damage. You can use this mechanic to balance the Notes within the party.

Torrent Duet: Abyssal Nappo summons speakers to unleash a large-scale wave attack. Players can only see danger zones that match the color of their own Note. When such a player enters the safe zone, the Note above their head will flash to indicate it. Tips: If danger zones are visible, quickly move to the safe zone. The mark above the player's head can help guide teammates to safety. If danger zones are not visible, follow players with different Notes. On Master difficulty, both elemental attacks may occur at the same time, requiring players with different marks to work together to locate the overlapping safe zone.

Super Dance - Opening: Abyssal Nappo sways and dances, creating two-colored warning zones on the ground. After several beats, Nappo attacks one of the colored zones and grants players a shield of the opposite color. Tips: During the Opening phase of Super Dance, leaving the spotlight area will result in massive damage. Watch the warnings and avoid the attacks, then remember the color of your shield to handle upcoming mechanics.

Super Dance - Variation: Abyssal Nappo uses Notes to cast spells, summoning clones or sonic orbs. If clones appear, players should quickly focus fire or interrupt the clone whose color is opposite to their shield. If sonic orbs appear, players must use their shield to absorb sonic orbs of the same color, preventing subsequent attacks. Tips: Spread out in advance and quickly handle clones or sonic orbs according to your shield color.

Attribute Orb: Goblins have a chance to drop Attribute Orbs when defeated. Picking one up grants a significant attribute boost. Tips: Attribute Orbs are non-exclusive, meaning collecting different types will stack their effects.
Self-Destruct Robot: Adventurers must avoid self-destruct robots that charge in from all directions. Touching one triggers an explosion and causes damage.

Touch of Frost: A stacking status effect under extreme cold weather. Increases DMG taken from the boss. At 20 stacks, the player becomes frozen. Allies can rescue the frozen player by breaking the ice. Harsh Weather: There are four weather levels: Clear, Rain, Snow, and Blizzard. The stacking speed of Touch of Frost differs by weather condition. Tips: In Snow or Blizzard weather, team members must stay close together.

Zero-Degree Snowfield: Targets a player with shared DMG and summons the Zero-Degree Snowfield. All players are linked to the snowfield core and continuously gain Touch of Frost stacks. Breaking the link deals DMG. Tips: Quickly exit the area and group together to minimize the effect.

Void Corruption Afterimage: Xiolotl summons two Void Corruption Afterimages that lock onto two players. After a delay, they charge at their targets. All players along their path share the DMG. Tips: Others should quickly move into the line to help share the DMG. On higher difficulties, Void Corruption Afterimages are enhanced. Any single player hit twice by the Void Corruption Afterimages will be instantly killed.

Purifying Light: Tonatiuh summons a one-hit-kill purifying light wall that expands or contracts at a fixed speed. Tips: Use the rift at the right moment to evade the light wall. On Nightmare mode, the boss summons linked light walls, and players must teleport multiple times.

Radiant and Dark Crystals: The Radiant and Dark Crystals continuously feed energy to the boss. Both must be defeated simultaneously or they will regenerate. Breaking the crystals interrupts the boss's charge. Tips: On Hard+ mode, crystals have shields. Breaking them inflicts a matching elemental Vulnerable debuff to the players on the islands and spawns a rift. Both teams must coordinate to destroy the crystal shields and rotate groups to avoid stacking debuffs.

Territory Awareness: When King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike are within each other's territory, they deal damage to the opposing territory. Tips: The two tanks should position King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike within their respective areas.

Territory Defense: King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike will each mark a territory and deal heavy damage. If no player absorbs the damage, the territory will : Dealing heavy damage over time until the battle ends. Tips: Tanks should respond to the alert and move to the designated territories to absorb the damage.

Territory Banish: King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike each summons an orb within their own territory, along with corresponding interactable orbs on the battlefield. After 10 seconds, the orbs summoned by the bosses unleash heavy AoE damage in the direction of the interactable target orbs. Tips: Two players shall interact with the target orbs and pull them to the sides of the battlefield to prevent damage to the party.

Judgment Hour: King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike enter a duel of judgment. Each leaps back to their own territory before charging at the other. During this time, players can cast their vote for the king they support by standing in the corresponding territory. The king with the majority of votes will deal a percentage of the opponent's Max HP as damage and seize one of the opponent's territories. The king with a territory advantage gains increased Attack SPD while in their own territory. Tips: Assign each player's voting position in advance and support the king with lower HP to balance the fight.

Vow of Valor: King of Radiance - Sunfire charges a powerful attack against King of Azure - Moonstrike, dealing massive damage and global AoE damage after a delay. King of Azure - Moonstrike deploys a shield to protect itself. Tips: Break the shield summoned by King of Azure - Moonstrike and remain inside it to avoid taking damage.

Earthshatter Fist - Chain - Part 1: The Withered Illusory Bloom resonates with the elements, charging a powerful strike. Interrupting the casting of Breath of the Dead Soil prevents it from dealing devastating damage, but this will cause its energy to overflow onto nearby adventurers. Subsequently, it locks onto that player and continuously releases linear Terra attacks. Strategy: Assign players to four positions to interrupt the monster's cast. Guide the connecting lines away from the devices to prevent Terra from hitting them.

Earthshatter Fist - Chain - Part 3: The Stonehusk locks onto a Ruin Device, generating shareable AoE damage at its location. During this time, the device cannot be carried or moved. If all devices are successfully shared, the Withered Illusory Bloom will enter a weakened state. Strategy: At least 3 players must participate in sharing the damage. Be aware that multiple devices may need to be shared simultaneously.

Defense System: If a Ruin Device is hit by the Stonehusk's powerful skill, it triggers a defense system that causes a massive explosion affecting all players, dealing damage over time. Tips: Players carrying devices must maintain proper positioning to avoid attacks. Rotate protection duties if necessary. Players without protection duties should also prioritize avoiding the devices when dodging skills.

Earthshatter Fist: The Stonehusk locks onto a Legacy Device and releases a rectangular, shareable damage zone. During this time, the device cannot be moved or repositioned, and a required number of players must enter the area to soak the damage together. Tips: At least 5 players must participate in damage soaking to prevent the device from triggering its Defense System. This attack knocks players back a considerable distance. Take advantage of the terrain wisely to block the displacement.

Path of Advance: Withered Bloomshard smashes through the walls and advance deeper into the ruins. The path ahead is infested with Illusory Blooms. When the Stonehusk approaches them, they detonate, dealing heavy damage and causing knockback to players. Tips: Assign some players to move ahead and clear the Illusory Blooms along the path, while the remaining players carry the Legacy Devices to suppress the Stonehusk and continue the advance.

Valley of Final Stand: Withered Bloomshard reaches the depths of the ruins and begins casting Rock of Ruin. If the cast completes, it will deal fatal damage to all players. The boss's shield must be shattered before the cast finishes. While fighting on elevated platforms, be cautious of knockback attacks to avoid falling to your death. Tips: Use interaction points to leap down onto the platform and burst down the boss's shield. Take advantage of stone walls for cover to avoid being launched off the high ground.

Judgment Hour - Hard: King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike enter a duel of judgment. Each leaps back to their own territory before charging at the other. During this time, players can cast their vote for the king they support by standing in the center of the corresponding territory. The king with the majority of votes will deal a percentage of the opponent's Max HP as damage and seize one of the opponent's territories. Players who don't vote will take damage over time for 10 seconds. The king with a territory advantage gains increased Attack SPD while in their own territory. Tips: Pre-assign voting positions and plan the number of voters to support the king with lower HP to balance the fight. If the group cannot be split evenly, tanks should abstain from voting to absorb damage.

Territorial Purge: King of Radiance - Sunfire and King of Azure - Moonstrike will each mark a territory, which will inflict shared damage. If no player absorbs the damage, the territory will be , dealing massive damage to all players that lessens with distance. Tips: 5 players should respond to the alert and move to the designated territories to absorb the damage.

Locked Domain: Once combat begins, the boss activates four light barriers, dividing the area into separate rooms. Each section becomes an independent space, and adventurers cannot damage the boss from across rooms. During the fight, each room gradually charges with energy until it is destroyed by electrical energy. Tips: Focus your attacks within a single room, and move to the next before it is destroyed.

Boundary Breach: Whenever a player passes through a light barrier, it triggers a destabilizing explosion that deals damage to all players. Strategy: Cross the barriers in staggered groups during the fight to avoid triggering excessive damage all at once.

Interference Construct: When an adventurer passes through a light barrier, a Mech Illusion is summoned in the corresponding room. There are two types: the melee-type Mech Illusion I, which applies a continuous HP loss debuff to its target through rapid attacks; and the ranged-type Mech Illusion V, which applies an ATK reduction debuff to all adventurers, and on Nightmare difficulty, it expands a domain that provides damage reduction to monsters. Tips: Guard Class Adventurers should enter the room first to draw aggro. Interrupt the weakening and defensive skills cast by Mech Illusion V.

Illusion - Terminus Singularity: The Remnant summons several cores charged with destructive energy across the arena. After a short duration, these cores detonate, dealing devastating damage to all adventurers and causing a total party wipe. Tips: Use the Annihilation Beam to destroy the energy cores before they detonate.

Annihilation Beam: The Remnant targets three adventurers in the arena, linking them with tethers. After a short delay, laser emitters spawn at the targeted adventurers' locations, firing beams along the tether paths. These beams deal heavy damage to any adventurers in their path but also destroy the energy cores. Tips: Targeted adventurers must position themselves so the tethers pass through the energy cores, causing the lasers to destroy them before they detonate.

Illusory Sync: The Remnant summons an illusion of itself and synchronizes with it to charge up energy. Both then unleash arena-wide attacks with damage that falls off over distance. Strategy: Guard Class Adventurers should lure the Remnant to the edge of the room beforehand to leave enough space to mitigate the fall-off damage. Move away from the main Remnant first, and then away from the illusion.

Illusion - Obliteration Railgun: The boss targets adventurers in sequence. When the countdown ends, the railgun strikes and damages platforms. A platform will completely collapse if it is damaged twice. Tips: Stack the railgun strikes in a controlled area and without falling with the platforms. Avoid leaving too many cracked platforms, as they will later be destroyed by the boss's Disintegration Shockwave skill. On Hard mode and above, the railgun descends faster, and players targeted in different waves must not stand on the same platform.

Disintegration Shockwave: The boss gathers energy and unleashes a powerful explosion, completely destroying all cracked platforms. Tips: This explosion's damage falls off with distance. Move as far away as possible to mitigate the damage.

Twin Sentinels: The boss summons two Mech Sentinels in the arena. The Sentinels continuously charge energy and unleash an explosion when fully charged, destroying the platform beneath them. On Hard difficulty and above, the Sentinels buff each other when they are close together. The boss will only re-enter the fight once the Sentinels are defeated. Tips: Adventurers must split into two teams and lure the Mech Sentinels onto separate platforms until they are defeated.

Divine Scale - Preset Return: The boss summons four spacetime rifts in the arena. Interacting with them will teleport all players to the interaction point when the countdown ends. Strategy: Interact appropriately according to the mechanics to dodge critical attacks.

Divine Scale - Causality Warp: The boss randomly summons two delayed AoE strikes that knock players back. Tips: If adventurers need to switch platforms, they should stand close to the damage zone facing their desired landing spot. If not switching platforms, be careful not to get knocked off the platform.

Gathering Life Skills include Botany, Mineralogy, and Gemology . When a life skill is first unlocked, you receive 3 Mastery points, which are shared across all life skills. You gain 1 additional point per 300 Focus consumed .

Gathering targets are divided into Focused and Regular. Regular doesn't consume Focus, but its products are untradeable-mainly used for crafting gear and furniture. Select an unlocked gathering target and use Track to view its location.

When you are within range of a gathering item, a gathering icon indicating its type will appear above it. Approach it to trigger an interaction button and begin gathering. There are two gathering modes: Focused and Regular . Focused consumes Focus , while Regular does not. All gathering activities grant EXP for the corresponding gathering classes, but the final rewards vary based on the method used.

Crafting Life Skills include Smelting, Culinary, Alchemy, Gemcrafting, Artisanry , and Weaving . When a life skill is first unlocked, you receive 3 Mastery points, which are shared across all life skills. You gain 1 additional point per 300 Focus consumed .

Recipes are divided into the Focused and Regulars. Regulars do not consume Focus but produce untradeable results. Furniture must be crafted at the Crafting Station in the Homestead. Here you can only view recipes and unlock requirements. Select an unlocked recipe and go to start tracking the Crafting Station location for that life skill.

Once you're near the target, an interaction button will appear. Open the crafting interface and view the unlocked recipes and required materials. If you have enough materials, use the Craft button below to create the item and gain Skill EXP. Some crafting recipes consume Focus during production, while others require no Focus.

Strange. Very strange. This city-once so powerful-has been reduced to ruin. The destruction is clear. The damage to these homes is unmistakably the result of war. How could a city under the protection of the Divine fall to such devastation? Was there an enemy more powerful than the Bapharian Divines? No... that's impossible. The truth must lie beyond what is apparent, and I am determined to uncover it.

The Merchant Guild scrambles to assess the mounting losses. According to prior agreements, this disaster will likely spark serious disputes... All we can do now is pray-to escape this sea alive.

Alician calendar, June 19, Year ■■■ The great pirate, Heathcliff Stormwrath, is now buried at sea. Now, there is only Orlando the cobbler. Facing the seabreeze of Asterleeds. Repenting. Greed was our downfall. We could have had a bright future. Aria, Gwen, Lorian... all buried at sea. We originally gathered for this jewel, yet we were torn apart because of it... As a captain, I was useless. Couldn't secure the jewel nor protect my companions... A pirate's honor has faded away with the past. I hope the fleet never finds me. Alician calendar, June 18, Year ■■■ The sun in Asterleeds is warm. But there are some dark corners that even the warmest sunlight cannot reach. Even after so many years, with a new family, a new identity. Those events are still etched in my mind. Like the curse on the Abyssal Eye, it follows me like a shadow. Always at the most difficult, most critical moments... It lands the fatal blow. Alician calendar, June 17, Year ■■■ It's that time again. Every year on these few days, I have that dream. I always return to that cave. Reliving the moment I climbed the highest reef and drifted along the current...

To those who seek the Abyssal Eye! Heed my words! The great pirate Heathcliff briefly possessed it. But even with my status, I couldn't suppress its evil power! First, the ship was wrecked, and we fell into this underwater sac cave. Then the monsters of the deep were drawn to it! My crew, my treasure, all swallowed whole... Avenge me and finish what I could not! If you can slay that sea monster, the jewel is yours. (Below is a roughly drawn map, with a dotted line ending in an X.) The monster's lair To summon it, you need the heavy scent of many skyfish. Don't ask me how I know. I don't want to relive my failed revenge.

Have you ever noticed those travelers known as Scavengers? They refuse to be bound by the mundane world, wandering freely like the wind. They carry their entire belongings in bulging packs, hurrying through alleys and vanishing quietly into the crowds. Their lives are like fallen leaves drifting in the wind, brushing past the world, free yet lonely. My name is Zek, and I'm journeying across the continent of Regnus as a scavenger. After a long trek, my companions and I finally arrived at the Asteria Plains. We heard of a mysterious forest there called the Duskdye Woods . We wanted to explore it while visiting some fellow scavenger friends who live there. However, that forest is full of dangers, with monsters roaming and Brigands lurking. For safety's sake, I'm now recruiting a brave adventurer to escort us. If you're interested, find the man with a giant backpack named Zek near the Pioneer Bureau. The contact phrase: "Hey Zek, found any treasures today?" Rest assured, the reward will be ample.
I didn't expect this. An adventurer. It seems my luck has turned.

Dear Ereka, Greetings to you. Victoria is a remarkably clever child. No one knows where she came from. I discovered her while delivering documents to the Corps. She was delirious from hunger, so I brought her home. She has stayed with me ever since. She excels at solving puzzles. She requested I include these details in my letter. While I don't understand their purpose, she insisted they would help you, so I've included them. She claims she can locate you. While I don't understand how she'll manage this feat, I recognize that even if she finds you, I might not be able to bring you back to the Duchy. Nevertheless, I maintain hope that she will find you. The day you were taken to sea, Hugues and I commandeered a fisherman's boat, but Duchy soldiers discovered us shortly after we set sail. Some claim raiders took you aboard their ship, while others insist you perished. Though this may now sound like excuses for my helplessness and inaction, Ereka, even without knowing the complete situation, I have always stood ready to be your companion. Or your accomplice. Perhaps you've forgotten, but before your departure, you scattered nuts across the yard to feed those rarely-seen birds. The remaining seeds took root in the soil and astonishingly developed into beautiful vining plants bearing new fruit. I've included one of these fruits with this letter. Should you receive it, it will serve as my eyes. Hoping to return to your side, Lloyd

The Golem is a mysterious device left behind by the Bapharian Divines. It's made of an unknown alloy, and its activation mechanism remains a mystery to humanity. Despite this, its extraordinary abilities, such as energy emission and environmental manipulation, have made it a prized treasure among archaeologists and black market traders alike. In most cases, a Golem remains dormant. However, it can briefly awaken when disturbed by impacts or energy interference. Its active period typically lasts from a few minutes to several hours. Reports suggest that when awakened, the Golem prioritizes the protection of delicate targets, such as specific objects or ecological zones. It responds only defensively to aggression and returns to the stationary state once the threat has passed. Additionally, the Golem appears to be pre-programmed to attack humans, making it extremely dangerous. Due to its rarity and enigmatic nature, the Golem has become a prized collectible among the wealthy, often reaching astronomical prices on the black market. However, following several tragic incidents where the Golem unexpectedly activated and caused significant casualties, the Creed has officially banned its trade.

Scarlet: Tonight, as I ran my fingers over the amber hairpin you left behind in the Stargazing Tower, the distant chime of the Creed's bell rang out-suddenly, I was swept back to your days in Byrnhald. I still can't understand it-how could that boy's naive promise move you to follow him into crumbling ruins, gnawing on dried bread in the wilderness, all while risking your life? If it were excitement you craved, I would have donned a gladiator's armor and dueled beneath your window till sunrise. If it were poetry you loved, I, a graduate of the Royal Academy, could have drowned your tent beneath a sea of sonnets. But no-you chose that lunatic who crouches among rubble, caked in mud and rust, chasing after moldy remnants of a forgotten past. Three marriage proposals from royal princesses sit unopened on my desk-and I've turned every one of them down. Don't mistake it. I'm simply waiting to see the look on your face when regret finally finds you. Baron Ravenkraw

(A fantasy novel about the brilliant artisan Mason, who falls from the prestigious position of chief technician to a humble boiler repairman, only to rise again in a powerful comeback. The book's captivating details about the creation of intricate instruments draw readers in, building a world where social status is determined by the mastery of craftsmanship. Interestingly, it seems that the character Mason might actually exist in real life in Asterleeds.)

Want to bond with your cat? Ever wonder what your cat is thinking when they are not eating? Then you need this practical guide: "How to Communicate with Your Kitty." This collection of basic cat expressions was compiled by the editor after years of running a pet club and interacting with thousands of cats. It covers a wide range of common feline behaviors and vocalizations-an essential guide for any cat lover. Basic Feline Vocalizations Meow-: I'm here. Meow-purr: I agree. Meow-meh (with tail swishing toward the desired direction): Come here. Meow-aww: I'm hungry. Purr-mrrr (with tail held high): I'm happy. Toot, toot (with tail slapping the ground): "I'm not happy." Feline Needs & Moods Purr, meow-meh (with tail tapping the ground): I don't know. Ask the human. Aww, purr (with tailing swaying): Don't bother me. Aww, purr- (with head lifted, trying to headbutt your nose): I'm really hungry. Aww, purr, grrr- (with back arched, fur puffed): I feel dangerous. Grrr-mrrr, aww: My paws are itchy.

Volume I: Complete Record of Attacks 1.1 First Attack: Sewer Assault Scene: The bodies of two Asterleeds Defense Corps soldiers were discovered in the sewer. The fatal injuries were deep neck punctures. The bodies were arranged in a kneeling posture, facing the direction of the Corps headquarters. The weapon used was a standard-issue Defense Corps firearm (Serial No. Gun-1079, originally assigned to the deceased soldier, Ryan Clough). Internal Corps Report: "Preliminary assessment indicates a retaliatory strike by the violent group 'The Hobos'. It is recommended to suppress the news to prevent public panic. " 1.2 Second Incident: Arena Town Theater Assault Witness Testimony (excerpt from Thomas' notes, a reporter at Ocean Hill Evening News): "During the third act of 'The Nobles of Byrnhald', the protagonist's wings suddenly ejected shards of gears. Defense Corps soldier Thomas, seated nearby, was struck and seriously injured. Upon investigating the control panel, a modified firearm was found lodged in it, with the handle inscribed 'Legacy Knight No. 1'. " Technical Analysis (from Artisan Guild's report): "The weapon was a modified training firearm issued to the Defense Corps. The training module appears to have been replaced with a high-damage combat module." 1.3 Final Showdown: The Bell Tower Duel Testimony from Surviving Defense Corps Soldier (Audio Recording No. 102, name omitted for safety reasons): "It was a man wearing an iron mask, his right arm moving too swiftly to be human... Soldier Adeline fought him, and in the end, she used Ryan's old sidearm to shoot through Ryan's chest. That's when Ryan finally fell. But at that moment... I heard Ryan's body make the sound of metal being pierced. " Autopsy Report: "The killer's right body had been modified with an unknown module, and a metal plate had been attached to his face. The left side of his face matched that of Ryan Clough. Ryan's heart was absent from the body."

Beyond research fields, the Artisan Guild also has a dedicated promotion system to reflect an artisan's professional level. As your level advances, you'll have different titles. This is a respect for seniority and a way to maintain order in the Artisan Guild. Artisan titles are typically divided into five ranks: Apprentice, Journeyman, Artisan, Expert, and Master. At the Apprentice level, you'll mainly be learning under an artisan mentor. Those who lack talent, have a poor attitude, or can't endure hardship will be given a Grade C evaluation by the mentor and eliminated outright. After completing your apprenticeship, you'll need to choose a specialization from Architecture, Legacy, Engine, and Forging based on your interests, strengths, and circumstances and join a corresponding research group. The Guildmaster will then issue you a formal Artisan Certificate, officially marking the beginning of your artisan career. From then on, you'll undergo periodic evaluations by your group's leadership, who will assess your skill proficiency and assign a ranking accordingly. Most of the full-fledged artisans you see around the Artisan Guild are in the Journeyman-Artisan stage. But take note: artisan ranks are never determined by years of experience. Advancement requires constant skill refinement, the completion of research tasks, or the creation of original works. Over time, your abilities will improve, and you'll evolve from Artisan to Master. At the Expert level, your role shifts from a follower to a leader and initiator. The guild hopes that Experts will guide apprentices and junior artisans, encouraging them to explore the unknown of their field. Therefore, Expert is usually the highest honor an artisan can attain unless someone achieves a major contribution (which often requires luck). Master-level artisans are extremely rare. Only those with widely recognized inventions or landmark contributions to their field are granted the title of Master. A Master may even hold more influence than the Guildmaster. At that point, you've entered a whole new realm as a Master Artisan's responsibilities go beyond just technique. Every action a Master takes, including their invention, research direction, and even their daily habits, is watched and followed by countless others. Among these followers are admirers, strangers, and even enemies. Each Master Artisan represents a transformative force. Their work and life have, in one way or another, shaped the destiny of Asterleeds. Some have even caused upheaval across all of humanity. Because artisans hold the sharpest blade of human reason. To hone the tool that can shape the world is the true purpose of an artisan.

As we all know, Master is the highest title for an artisan. But what kind of artisan truly deserves the title of Master? Or rather, what qualifies one to be selected for it? One belief is that the person must have made a significant contribution to the Artisan Guild or led a team that has won multiple Expo awards. But that's not necessarily the case. The Artisan Guild's closed and rigid system has, in some ways, stifled innovation. ... Years ago, the guild wasn't so hostile or dismissive toward Imagine Seeds. Back then, a Master-level artisan, Mason Stonecutter, was a strong advocate for Imagine Seed research. Mason believed these seeds could eventually outshine Bapharian Legacies in versatility. Mason is a legend among artisans. Some say he was taught directly by Webber, and others claim he was Ted's mentor. But what truly secured his place as a Master was his core theory for modifying Bapharian Legacies. At the time, Legacy artisans were stuck, unable to crack the core mechanisms of the Legacies. Mason, ahead of his time, proposed a bold alternative: Set aside the core tech temporarily and use Legacies as modular components for real-world applications. This idea massively advanced Legacy modification, leading artisans to re-engineer Legacies into tools for daily life, combat, and transport. The adoption rate of Legacies in Asterleeds now has reached an all-time high, even overloading the Webber Energy Network. Yet the current framework for Legacy modification still follows Mason's ideas. Even so, Mason faced growing internal skepticism despite his immense contributions to the Artisan Guild. As mentioned earlier, Mason placed great value on the study of Imagine Seeds. Later, he abandoned his Legacy research career and devoted himself entirely to Imagine Seed studies. However, the research yielded no tangible results after consuming vast funding. Eventually, the Guild and Mason had a falling out. The then-Guildmaster cut off funding for the Imagine Seed project. Enraged, Mason left the Artisan Guild and founded the Imagine Research Institute, where he continues his research in that field. However, his influence is no longer what it once was.

The Artisan Guild hosts its own grand event: the annual Artisan Expo. Held every year since the end of the Asterleeds Independence War, the Artisan Expo is now approaching its seventh installment. What kind of brilliant inventions will appear this year? 1. 4th-Gen Engram Engine The Engram Engine is a reliable gold-medal contender. Widely used and steadily improving with each version, this small engine holds endless potential. It's been making significant contributions to various industries of Asterleeds. According to Engine artisans, the Engram Engine still has much room for growth. However, the third-generation engine was so spectacular and has already won multiple awards. Judges may want to give other innovations a chance this year. After all, the Expo is open to the public, and if the award results feel too predictable, it could dampen public enthusiasm. Regardless, the Engram Engine remains a solid fallback for the gold medal. 2. Modular Luminous Unit. A remarkable Legacy module that can shape light however you want. It can focus into a powerful beam or disperse into a wide, illuminating field. According to artisans, with sufficient energy, the beam could stretch from the tallest spire in Asterleeds' diocese to the Ruins of Andra City. Moreover, this module has immense expansion potential. Some artisans propose embedding data in the beam for instant information transmission. Others suggest strengthening the beam to turn it into a weapon piercing heavy armor and shields. 3. Hypnosis Ray A bizarre invention that can instantly make a creature collapse into sleep. Forging artisans accidentally synthesized a crystal with hypnotic properties. In darkness, the crystal charges itself. Upon exposure to light, it releases a dazzling wave of energy that induces sleep in everyone present. This wave is so penetrative that even closed eyes can't block it. It has promising application potential, such as subduing dangerous people, deterring monsters, and even becoming a standard-issue weapon for the army. However, the Hypnosis Ray Crystal is still in the testing phase. Its instability and unavoidable effect make it difficult to apply in real-world scenarios. Imagine a guard pulling the trigger to subdue a suspect, only to collapse first because he forgot to wear protective gear. The scene would be quite hilarious.

In Year ■■■, Alician calendar, a master of improvisational performance, dressed in black, completed an epic performance on Ocean Hill. This performance was unprecedented and likely to never be surpassed, leaving a lasting impression on all who witnessed it. He began with mime techniques, effortlessly slipping into the Ocean Hill hall. Next, he warmed up on the first floor with stunning sleight-of-hand, pocketing several councilors' proposals. Then, without taking the stairs or using any wires, he ascended to the second floor of Ocean Hill. The performance hit its climax as he reached the second-floor terrace. He pulled out a stage dagger and, before anyone could react, stabbed it into the back of the Energy Committee representative right before everyone's eyes. The audience froze, then erupted in shocked screams. Just five steps away, 4 Asterleeds Defense Corps soldiers joined the performance with their stunning acting skills: one kicked over a lampstand, another pretended his sword was stuck in its sheath, one embraced the carpet, and the last dramatically kissed the assassin's heel in restraint. This breathtaking spectacle, which lasts 127s, was immortalized by a painter on the second floor with his brush. The painting was later published in Coast Daily and won numerous awards.

During the spirit-burning rite of the Celebration of the Fiery Moon, I witnessed High Priestess Yaretsi set the bone offering aflame, seeking a divination for the tribe's future. But just as the flames licked the edges, a loud crack rang out. The fang split open, and the fire abruptly died. Such a sign is considered an extremely ill omen, foretelling grave misfortune for the tribe. As an assistant priest, I was at a loss. I could only look helplessly at Yaretsi, whose face had gone pale as paper. She, too, seemed shaken. Perhaps it was her first time facing such a result. We sat in silence. Outside, the tribe danced joyfully around the bonfire under the guidance of the Summer Priestess. Laughter and warmth filled the air, while we, only a few feet away, sat frozen in dread. I glanced at the priestess's earrings. Delicate crescent bone ornaments, swaying faintly in the eerie light of the extinguished flame. The two of us sat motionless, and for a moment, it felt as though time itself had stopped. At last, Yaretsi broke the silence. She grabbed the shattered spirit bone and forced out a few words through clenched teeth: "Prepare the rites. I will perform a deep communion. " Deep communion! The moment I heard those words, a chill ran down my spine. That ritual is known to consume one's very life force, said to summon the ancestors themselves to deliver their decree. What dreadful omen had Yaretsi glimpsed in the flames to warrant such desperate action?

This was one of the most serious derelictions of duty in the history of the Kanamia Tribe. On a night in the Month of Frost, sentry Hakrei was tricked into drinking a specialty drink offered by outsiders. Intoxicated, he passed out, leaving the Forbidden Land unguarded, allowing a group of desecrators to break in and steal the tribe's sacred relic. When Hakrei awoke and realized what had happened, it was too late. The priests had no choice but to enter the sacred grounds and inspect the damage. They discovered that the Sacred Spring, used in healing rites and the source of the spring itself, had been taken. The entire tribe was thrown into alarm. The Elders traveled personally to Asterleeds to request aid. With the help of the Defense Corps, the culprits were intercepted at the port as they tried to load the relic onto a ship. The thieves turned out to be members of the black market group known as Brazer, who had recently disguised themselves as merchants to get close to Hakrei. His lack of judgment allowed them to act. As punishment, Hakrei was permanently stripped of his title as a sentry and sentenced to roll five thousand hides. His family, too, faced social exclusion and remains shunned to this day. Thankfully, the Sacred Spring source was recovered. Had it been lost, the Kanamians would no longer have had the dignity to face their ancestral spirits. Let this stand as a warning to all: never neglect your duty, and never trust the words of strangers.

The White Wolf of the Kanamia Tribe is not merely a mythic creature of legend. In recent decades, there have been numerous sightings: accounts backed by scrolls, oral history, and a wealth of documentation. Most prevailing explanations take an agnostic stance: perhaps this mythological being truly existed, appearing in the form of a species unknown to us. Yes, invoking the supernatural, the divine, or an undiscovered lifeform is a tidy solution. But doing so merely plants a sign that reads: "Unknown. Do not enter. " And we've seen too many signs like that already. What I offer here is not idle speculation, but a hypothesis built on observation. It's one step toward the river's dark and unfathomable depths. That is: the White Wolf that once protected Kanamia Tribe may very well have been an Imagine Seed. You don't believe me? Then why is it that nearly every record of the White Wolf shows it arriving at just the right moment! Howling valiantly or saving the tribe at its darkest hour? What a miraculous coincidence! The Kanamians will, of course, say: "The ancestral spirit knows when its people suffer, and sends the White Wolf." A beautiful sentiment. A valid one. But it's only one of many possibilities. Let us explore the others. Let us seek reason Why is there no mention of the White Wolf's everyday life? Where did it sleep? What did it eat? Where are its droppings? Why is there nothing? It's as if the creature came from another world altogether. If it truly hailed from beyond, why appear as a wolf? What form did it take before that? And why did it vanish just before the tribe's greatest crisis? This ancestral spirit that saved the Kanamians a hundred times before-why abandon them when they needed it most? If the tribe committed some blasphemy that drove it away, there should be records. But so far, none exist However, if the White Wolf was in fact an Imagine Seed, everything falls into place. The tribe, knowingly or not, may have triggered the seed. It manifests as this fearsome, supernatural being. And when the seed's projected duration ends, the White Wolf disappears, leaving behind no trace of a physical life. As for its disappearance before the war? That might suggest the seed was lost in a time of internal conflict. Or that the Kanamians never learned to activate it consistently. After all, even the Pioneer Bureau hasn't figured out how to fully "play" with these things. Of course, the "Seed Hypothesis" opens up a more terrifying possibility: What if there was a real giant White Wolf, and the Imagine Seed merely recorded it faithfully? Even if the theory is imperfect, the pursuit of truth must follow the evidence-not leap over it by stamping "Unknown" across the page. That kind of thinking, in itself, is a desecration. After all, when you see the edge... you've already crossed it.

You ask me who I prefer doing business with? Not the Merchant Guild. Those folks have more tricks than a bird has feathers. Street vendors? Forget it. They'll haggle over every last coin. The Fishers' Guild is alright. Honest folk. But I don't deal in seafood, so not much overlap there. No, I prefer the scavengers. They're out on the plains every day with a heavy pack on their back, always bumping into rocks, thorns, and bad luck, so they've got to stock up on my medical supplies. They always need firestarters, and more often than not, they top off their lamp oil or grab a coil of sturdy rope before heading out again. And the best part? They don't haggle. Ever. They hand over a list, drop the coin, grab their gear, and walk. Now that-that's what I call refreshing. What? You're asking where they get their money? Okay, fine... I've done a little digging. Don't give me that look. I worry too, alright? Last thing I want is the Defense Corps knocking on my door while I'm serving tainted coin. Turns out, some of these scavengers are master leatherworkers. That fine leather coat worn by a city noble? Might've been stitched together by one of these folks. Others make their coin collecting junk on the road-stuff most people toss out-and either sell it to passing merchants or peddle it here in the city. And you know what? After they clean it up and patch it together, it actually looks... kinda nice. Tempting, even. And if all else fails... Well, rumor has it some scavengers come from money. Playing scavenger is just their version of "living free." Not my place to judge. Now, sure, there are a few who swipe things now and then. Lazy types who want a shortcut. But around here, us merchants have a system. One glance, a raised eyebrow, and we know who to keep an eye on.

Scavengers, take heed: Yes, there are wartime Legacies scattered along this beach-modules, armor, even unopened supply crates. But beside every "treasure," you may find an unexploded shell, a malfunctioning relic, or a cloud of poison gas. Marco. Eri. Jokebo. They once walked this shore, confident as you are. Now, all that remains of them... are their names. Before you step forward, ask yourself: Can you tell a dud shell from a supply cache? Can you recognize the sickly-sweet stench of toxic mist? Can you guarantee that come sunrise, your friends won't be reading your name to an empty sky? Mourners, this is not your altar: True remembrance belongs in the Statue of the Hero. If your grief burns unquenched... Write to the Council! (Scrawl with the angriest pen, the clumsiest letters, and ask them when they plan to clean up this battlefield rot.) Tourists, eyes up: The giant golem arm is the safest place for a scenic view. You'll see the whole battlefield-and still have all your limbs to go home with. Still tempted to touch the sands below? Think of the ones who vanished, whose bodies grew suddenly half as light. Cove, Survivor of Asterleeds Independence War

Legend has it that two hundred years ago, followers of the witch Hruga appeared on the Bahamar Highlands and unleashed a terrifying ​Void Engram, seeking to annihilate humanity... At that time, humans were no match for Hruga. After one crushing defeat after another, human civilization stood on the brink of annihilation. In a moment of desperation, the Creed guided emissaries of the Bapharian Divines to the highlands. With the help of the deities, Hruga was finally defeated and sealed. However, her power scattered across the Bahamar Highlands, severely disrupting the flow of Engram​ here. The most immediate manifestation is the growth of Illusory Bloom—a sinister crystalline with an otherworldly appearance, still widespread across the highlands. Its crystalline shell is nearly impervious, with remarkable regenerative ability, making it almost impossible to destroy completely. Illusory Bloom thus stands as a lasting mark of that ancient war, continuing to threaten the lives of the local inhabitants.

The Illusory Bloom is a dangerous flower found throughout the entire highlands—its colors vibrant, yet hiding a deadly threat. Those who draw near it are affected by its unique Engram​, which instantly disrupts the flow of their Bio-Engram. Their inner anxieties and fears are then amplified, trapping them in the most terrifying illusions—unable to break free. This has nothing to do with courage, because the terror comes from your own imagination. Whatever you fear—fear so deeply it cuts to the bone—the more that fear grips you. In short... there is no escape. This overwhelming terror deals near-fatal damage to the body. For those physically frail, death may come on the spot. Yet the most frightening aspect is that anyone ensnared by the illusion completely loses control of their own body. Only a clear-headed companion can drag you away from the bloom's vicinity; otherwise, the illusions will continue to assault you until your mind and strength are entirely exhausted. Even for those who manage to escape, the damage to their psyche is often permanent. In the years that follow, those nightmares will cling to them like a restless shadow—surging forth at the height of their happiness, or murmuring ceaselessly in the silence of midnight...

To survive in the mines, you must strictly follow these rules: Rule 1: If you're working and suddenly a pebble flies from behind you, do not turn around! Do not turn around! Do not turn around! Rule 2: If an extra shadow of yourself appears under the searchlight, do not run. Hold your breath immediately. Rule 3: If you see a minecart moving on its own along the tracks and glowing red, do not approach it, and never look directly inside the carriage! Rule 4: If a miner's pickaxe suddenly lifts into the air on its own, step aside instantly and give up your digging spot. Rule 5: If you hear dripping sounds coming from within the rock wall, whistle a full miner's tune immediately. Do not let the dripping sync with your heartbeat. Rule 6: If you're alone and hear someone clearly call your full name, check your ID tag at once and confirm your name. Final Rule: Keep this in mind that you always descend into the mines alone. If you suddenly hear someone speak to you, no matter what they ask, no matter how familiar the voice sounds, do not answer! Keep your eyes straight ahead and continue mining until the shift-change bell rings. Please keep these rules in mind, and good luck—If anything goes wrong, check whether your shadow is still following you normally...

Dearest Anna, You've never seen a forest like it! The trees are so tall they seem to tear the sky open, and the fog is so thick it clings to your face like cream. The Pioneer Bureau calls it the Slumberdream Valley. Me... I think it's more like a place that just swallows people's sleep. You'll definitely laugh—I actually dozed off while I was lost in there! When I woke up, I was covered in a cold sweat. I'd just dreamed that the tree roots were moving, as if they were about to entangle me. But don't worry, I got out of there with a cool head and a bit of luck. It's just that the feeling of the nightmare seems to stick in my head even after waking up. I can't shake it off. Ah, speaking of which, I have to admit... I haven't dared to tell anyone else about this. I'm afraid they'd laugh at me for being a coward. You'd better not laugh at me. By the way, if I can really overcome all this, that counts as part of my training as an adventurer, right? Your brother, Federico, who's trying to be more reliable

Riddle: Who is the boss of the armed force occupying the Ruins of Andra City, Dark Mist Legion ? Denvel Taltraud You wretched worms Answer: Denvel Note: He's a grim Byrnhald soldier, motivated by his discontent with the outcome of the Asterleeds Independence War. He refused the summons of the Grand Duke of Byrnhald​... And so, he occupied the Ruins of Andra City, plotting to completely crush Asterleeds.

Scarna, a down-and-out treasure hunter, unexpectedly obtains half of an ancient scroll marked "Divine Ruins." To unravel the secret of his ancestors, lost during their own hunt for treasure, he gathers companions with extraordinary skills—a genius artisan well-versed in mechanisms, an old scholar familiar with ancient texts and ciphers, and a highly skilled retired soldier. The four-person squad sets off from a dangerous cliffside area. Along the way, they pass through poisonous miasma mazes in secret rainforests and the claustrophobic cabins of deep-sea shipwrecks, journeying through seemingly hopeless dangers to reach their destination—the place where the treasure is hidden. They must not only decipher the exquisite mechanisms left by their predecessors and fend off attacks from beasts and nature, but also face off in life-and-death struggles with other treasure hunters coveting the hoard. During the journey, every treasure they discover hides forgotten secrets of history, and every crisis is accompanied by both trials and growth. As the truth gradually surfaces, they discover that what lies behind the treasure is not just wealth, but the forgotten legacy of a civilization, and a mission to protect it...

Dear Thaddeus, are you doing well in Byrnhald? Have you heard the recent rumors? Yes, the ones about that treasure... I'm guessing you already know. I'm writing to ask if you'd be willing to form a party with me and head to the Bahamar Highlands. With our skills, we can definitely win the day and claim this tantalizing treasure for ourselves... Our abilities are never in question—it's just that we happen to lack a little bit of luck. But a person can't be unlucky forever, and it's about time we caught a lucky break! I feel like this is our chance. If you're thinking the same thing, write back to me, and I'll pack my bags and come find you. Adventure novels are still missing a treasure-hunting duo with both courage and skill. I think it's time our names were written in them.

...That blue-and-yellow striped mutated Arachnocrab blocked the intersection of the mine tunnel like a heavy war chariot. I had never seen such a brazen monster. It didn't even try to hide when it saw us. Instead, it paced lazily through the crossroads, as if we were beneath its notice. We were still whispering about what to do when, in a flash, it charged right in front of us. Our shields splintered and folded like paper under its pincers. The rock walls resounded with a massive roar, like the sound of chitinous shells scraping against stone, or blades clashing against hard iron, so sharp it made my scalp tingle. Suddenly, someone cried out: It's a mutated Arachnocrab! Before their words even faded, the miner next to me dropped his pickaxe, only to be tackled by an Arachnocrab bursting from a nearby crevice. Screams echoed one after another. Our formation faltered completely, and we ran for our lives. The mine tunnel was littered with severed limbs, and fragments of torn weapons and armor...

...It's the fourteenth day, and still no rescue. Given how long we've been gone, the Legion should long since have sent someone looking for us. But only darkness lies in this mine tunnel. It's an irregularity that fills me with unease. I'm even starting to suspect that the last tragedy was an attack targeting the Legion. Could it be that something also happened... over at the main mine tunnel? I dare not think too much about it. Right now, the only light we have is the eerie glow of Crimson Marrow. The vein looks like it's breathing... Ram previously told me not to get too close to that thing—said it would make me lose my mind. But I am awake. Frighteningly awake. I know I will survive. Because I discovered that I have the ability to evade Arachnocrab attacks. Ram didn't—that's why he was dragged away by that Arachnocrab. A mutated one smashed down from above, its stinger piercing his shoulder armor like a nail through wood. Before the scream even fully escaped his mouth, he was dragged back into the rocks. Since then, I understood: if I want to live, I can't think like a human. I have to think of myself as an Arachnocrab, become part of the Kahn Shaft. That's the only way to keep the Arachnocrabs from noticing me, and ensure I get to keep living. I have already avoided several attacks. But the Kahn Shaft seems to be expanding. More and more branches are appearing. Our people, on the other hand... are becoming fewer and fewer.

1. Origin and Effects of the Deep-Slumber Psychoscope: The Deep-Slumber Psychoscope is an external mental-tuning device originating from the Bapharian Divines, later modified by artisans. When an adventurer links with the Deep-Slumber Psychoscope, it stabilizes the mind, resisting hallucinations and awakening the adventurer's subconscious power, making them stronger. 2. Deep-Slumber Psychoscope Progression: The Psychoscope system is composed of the Deep-Slumber Psychoscope and the Illusion-Breaking Psychoscope. Each Psychoscope contains multiple Mind Projection areas. Adventurers can select and activate 1 area under each Psychoscope. Each Mind Projection area contains multiple Anchors of the Mind, Phantom Cursors, and Psychogram Imprint nodes (areas under the Illusion-Breaking Psychoscope do not have Psychogram Imprint nodes). By cultivating these nodes, adventurers can enhance their strength. 3. Applicable Environments: The effects of the Deep-Slumber Psychoscope apply in all combat environments, while the effects of the Illusion-Breaking Psychoscope apply only in the Slumberdream Valley.

Alician calendar, August ■■■, Year 600, Rainy Rain drums on the tent like a death knell. I remember Denvel saying: "A true commander fights for peace. Blind sacrifice is meaningless." He always used to say that, but now we're all lingering on the verge of death. I saw his armor stained red with my own eyes. Each red stain corresponded to a face that would never smile again. He now spends all day caressing that terrible weapon. More than once, I've stumbled upon him in the trenches, muttering the names of fallen comrades to the empty air. Over time, his obsession actually condensed into a visible crystal, like a teardrop-shaped piece of amber... The Imagine Seed traps him in his memories. But the enemy won't give us time to dream. During the surprise attack the day before yesterday, Denvel ordered the destruction of the civilian evacuation route. When the light of the explosion reflected on his face, I saw, for the first time, the devil's reflection in the Dominion eyes. This morning, I secretly slipped the Imagine Seed into his overcoat pocket. It was supposed to be the key to saving his last shred of humanity. But he dropped the water cup as if scalded, the crystal shards glinting faintly on the muddy ground like a small corpse. I dare not guess what was hidden in his final gaze. Was it disgust? Anger? Or... fear? This seed is about to sprout in my pocket. I must do something, before it's too late...

Vous et vos compagnons reconstituez les événements à partir du planning des relèves et confirmez qu'une mutinerie a eu lieu à la mine pendant une période non documentée. Ensuite, en suivant les indices, vous trouvez Breck qui, bien qu'il semble suivre le mouvement, a laissé derrière lui une clé des grottes de la mine. À l'intérieur de la grotte, vous trouvez un journal anonyme et apprenez que la moelle pourpre est extraite sur ordre du Grand-duc depuis au moins un an, et qu'un certain Klaus a été pris dans la tourmente pour sa loyauté envers ces ordres. Les indices finissent par pointer vers Devin. Ce n'est qu'en trouvant ce sergent, qui soutient toujours le commandant, que les fragments de la vérité pourront être assemblés afin de bloquer l'écoulement du minerai. Darya retourne d'abord à la zone de transfert pour s'occuper des mineurs, tandis que vous, Airona et Boyce suivez les rails des wagonnets jusqu'à la station de transport, prêts à continuer d'enquêter sur le réseau de contrebande et le cerveau qui se cache derrière.

Une page du livre de mémoire de Sabine, écrite lorsqu'elle s'est souvenue de l'affrontement. Elle était initialement destinée à Gaston, mais comme il pensait que ces souvenirs ne lui apporteraient que plus de douleur, Gaston l'a laissée à vos soins. La page indique : ———————————————————————————————————————————— ... Ce type, Edred, s'est vraiment impliqué avec la tristement célèbre mission Chou. Il prévoyait même d'utiliser les canaux de la guilde pour les aider à vendre leurs marchandises. Progressivement, j'ai réalisé que ce qu'il voulait était probablement plus que de simples Lunos. Mais Edred ne nous a jamais montré les comptes... Personne dans la guilde ne savait exactement ce qu'ils échangeaient. Plus tard, sa coopération avec la mission Chou a même attiré l'attention du Credo. Si elle était ignorée, ma guilde, la guilde que j'ai eu tant de mal à construire, serait ruinée. J'ai donc décidé de solliciter un soutien externe compétent auprès d'un aventurier actif dans cette zone. Je voulais que l'aventurier soit témoin du moment où j'ai démasqué Edred et l'ai forcé à remettre le sceau d'autorité de la guilde. Mais j'étais loin de me douter que son partenaire commercial était... la Société du Partage de Vision ! ... Par la suite, ma mémoire est floue. Je me souviens seulement qu'Edred semblait être une personne complètement différente. Ensuite... le temps a semblé s'arrêter. Une obscurité abyssale m'a presque engloutie, et c'est seulement en m'agrippant à ce bouton de manchette que j'ai réussi à conserver une once de conscience... C'était mon devoir. ... Quand ces deux-là sont apparus, le temps s'est remis à couler... Ils m'ont sauvée ! J'ai vu l'un d'eux repousser Edred avec une maîtrise de l'épée remarquable. L'autre a blessé le Miroir originel avec une arbalète de poing, et puis... ma tête s'est fendue de douleur, et j'ai de nouveau perdu connaissance. Quand je me réveillais de temps en temps, le monde s'était calmé. Ils ont dû me donner des soins de base, car mes blessures me faisaient moins mal. Celui avec l'arbalète de poing dispersait une poudre blanche, tandis que l'autre disait d'un ton sérieux : "Efface toute trace qui n'appartient pas aux lieux, et nettoie aussi la poudre." C'est tout ce dont je me souviens, mais il doit y avoir une conspiration plus large derrière Edred. Ma tête... me fait tellement mal... C'est comme si quelque chose m'empêchait de me souvenir... Empêchant la vérité de revenir... ———————————————————————————————————————————— Les notes se terminent brusquement. Le trait final a été écrit avec une telle force qu'il a déchiré le papier.

Boutique de boissons spéciales Nous sommes dévoués au riche sédiment et à l'arôme malté nés du brassage traditionnel, enchantés par les diverses saveurs révélées par des variétés d'orge uniques, et captivés par le caractère que chaque brassin tire de la météo, et même de l'humeur du brasseur. C'est notre passion. C'est la boisson spéciale traditionnelle d'Asterleeds. Mais c'est faux ! Ha ! Je parie que vous n'aviez même pas remarqué qu'on s'appelle la "Taverne Comme-Bon-Vous-Semble" ! J'ai écrit tout ce long paragraphe juste pour montrer à quel point ça fait du bien de se lâcher après avoir été si guindé ! Évidemment, le plus important dans une boisson, c'est qu'elle soit bonne, alors franchement, mettez-y ce que vous voulez ! Notre credo : la fantaisie est reine, le goût est roi ! (S'éclaircit la gorge) C'est fort, c'est sûr, mais pas assez synchro. Encore une fois : La-fantaisie-est-reine, le-goût-est-roi ! Ça, c'est mieux ! Et maintenant, voici le menu de la saison ! Menu de saison "Crevichampi arc-en-ciel" : une explosion de notes fruitées et colorées avec des nuances veloutées ! "Brume d'Asterleeds" : un mélange solide et traditionnel pour les amateurs de classiques. "Le baiser du maître de guilde des marchands" : passionné ! Authentique ! Populaire ! Une saveur intense qui vous monte à la tête ! "Le prêtre de la danse endiablée" : un mélange expérimental, pour les plus téméraires. "La tournée de la ville de l'arène pour trois spectateurs" : une expérience riche et cohérente, taillée pour les connaisseurs de niche.

An 601, Mois d'Auriramus La guerre dure depuis plus d'un an maintenant. Je suis le seul survivant de mon escouade d'origine. Valer est tombé lors de notre première escarmouche, tandis que les autres reposent encore dans la forêt de Kanamia... Je suis maintenant le capitaine d'une escouade d'une centaine d'hommes. J'ai gravi les échelons plus vite que presque n'importe qui, à l'exception des unités de première ligne. Mais je me demande, devrais-je me réjouir ? Père, j'ai toujours pensé que c'était cette petite épée en bois qui me portait chance, mais maintenant... elle est tachée d'écarlate depuis bien longtemps. Je ne sais pas si cette chance va durer. An 601, Mois de Nivadus Depuis la bataille dans la forêt de Kanamia, ma foi en la justesse de cette campagne a vacillé. Si les rebelles agissent vraiment comme le disait le Duc, en extorquant des richesses par l'oppression du peuple, et en contrôlant leur liberté par la violence, alors pourquoi les artisans d'Asterleeds risqueraient-ils leur vie si désespérément pour couvrir la retraite des rebelles ? Père, je t'ai écrit un jour que je me battais pour l'honneur et la justice. Mais qu'est-ce que l'honneur ? Qu'est-ce que la justice ? Père, je suis tellement perdu. Mais quoi qu'il arrive, je dois être responsable de mes soldats. Je dois les ramener à la maison.
